info.title: EdgePress Tenant API
info.description: Per-tenant CMS API. Authenticate every request with a personal access token: `Authorization: Bearer epat_...`. Create + manage tokens at `/admin/settings/api-tokens`.

tenant.description: Your tenant hostname (subdomain of edgepress.cc or a custom domain).

shopperSession.name: __Host-shop_session
shopperSession.description: Shopper session cookie (store tenants only). Set by POST /api/shop/login. For storefront browsers — PATs cannot obtain or use it. State-changing shopper requests must also echo the __Host-shop_csrf cookie's token in X-CSRF-Token.

cartToken.name: __Host-shop_cart
cartToken.description: Anonymous guest-cart token (store tenants only). Minted (HttpOnly, 256-bit CSPRNG) by the first guest POST /api/shop/cart. A bearer credential for that one cart on that one store — it never authenticates a shopper. Signed-in requests ignore it: a __Host-shop_session cookie always binds cart operations to the customer instead.

operationName.description: Operation to run when the document holds more than one.

GraphQLResponse.description: GraphQL envelope. Status is 200 even for failures — inspect `errors`.

is_layout.description: Store product only. 1 on the single seeded layout template (slug `layout`) whose site-header / page-slot / site-footer blocks wrap every storefront page when published. Cannot be created, defaulted, parented or deleted via the API; publish/unpublish it to turn the layout on/off.

system_key.description: Store product only. Read-only and seed-owned: marks a built-in page (cart, checkout, checkout-return, search, blog, blog-post, 404) that a migration-owned seed created and re-creates on every fan-out. Never client-settable — deliberately absent from both the create (POST /api/v1/templates) and update (PATCH /api/v1/templates/:id) field lists, so it can only be read, never written. `null` means an ordinary operator template. A non-null value changes several endpoints' behaviour: see DELETE, PATCH, POST .../unpublish, POST .../bulk and POST .../preview-token below.

custom_css.description: Store product only. Template-level custom CSS, emitted in a `<style data-source="template-css">` on every page rendered through this template (unscoped — the page is the operator's document). Max 8000 bytes. Rejected with the reason (`template_custom_css: <reason>`) when it contains @import, url() that is not a data: URI, expression(), `</style>` or non-printable bytes. Block-level `config.custom_css` on any block type that declares it follows the same rules, scoped to the block's root class; site-level CSS lives in `settings.theme.rawCss`.

publishedVersion.description: JSON snapshot of the template row taken at publish time

blockType.description: One of the types listed by GET /api/blocks

slug.description: Optional; generated from `name` when omitted. Must be unique across templates (409 on duplicate).

isDefault.description: true unsets any other default template of the same type

UpdateTemplateRequest.description: All fields optional; only supplied fields are updated.

slug.description: Must stay unique across templates (409 on duplicate)
Optional; generated from `name` when omitted. Must be unique within the template (409 on duplicate).

UpdateZoneRequest.description: All fields optional; only supplied fields are updated.

slug.description: Must stay unique within the template (409 on duplicate)

config.description: Validated against the block type's JSON Schema; violations return 400 with `validationErrors`

PatchBlockRequest.description: All fields optional; only supplied fields are updated. `config` keys are shallow-MERGED into the stored config, not a replacement.

config.description: Top-level keys merged into the stored config; the merged result is re-validated against the block type's JSON Schema

ReorderRequest.description: Array order becomes orderIndex 0..n. Pass `zoneIds` when reordering zones, `blockIds` when reordering blocks.

templateId.description: Template id to assign, or `null` to unassign (removes the page's template).

StoreUrlRedirect.description: URL preservation for a migrated catalogue (project 4). A row the engine (store-app/functions/utils/redirects.js) checks before answering a storefront 404. state is pending until the engine confirms to_path actually resolves (answers a non-cached 302 until then), then live (a cacheable 301) - the engine flips it, never the API. source names where the row came from: operator (added by hand here), migration:backfill (the one-time sweep over already-migrated products/categories), or migration:shopify / migration:woocommerce (written during an active catalogue migration) - it is also the key DELETE /api/v1/products/redirects?source= undoes by.

from_path.description: Normalised at write time: lowercased, query/hash stripped, trailing and repeated slashes collapsed. Unique per store.

StoreCategory.description: A store catalogue category. Categories form a tree via parent_id; deleting a parent detaches its children (parent_id becomes null).

product_count.description: Products directly in this category (join rows). Branch totals are the caller's to sum.

field_presets.description: Product detail fields every product in this category (and its subcategories) is asked for. null = none.

StoreProduct.description: A store catalogue product. price and compare_at_price are integer minor units in the product currency (1999 = 19.99). Category membership is stored in a join table; the single-product GET returns it as `categories`, an array of category ids.

price.description: Integer minor units. Never a float.

images.description: JSON array of image URLs, as a string.

stock.description: Units in stock, or null for NOT TRACKED (untracked products are never refused at checkout). 0 = tracked and sold out.

is_digital.description: 1 = digital product: when every line in the cart is digital, checkout skips the address form. It does not waive the delivery charge — use shipping_exempt for that.

shipping_exempt.description: 1 = never adds a delivery charge; free_over is judged on the non-exempt goods; an all-exempt cart records shipping_amount 0.

allow_oversell.description: Per-product permission to sell past stock (default 0 — every product behaves as it always has). With it set, checkout no longer refuses this product for insufficient stock: stock floors at 0 and each unit sold past it is added to backordered instead. It does NOT weaken the stock guard for any other product.

backordered.description: Units sold past stock and still owed to shoppers — never negative, and never written directly (checkout accrues it; cancelling or refunding pays it down BEFORE any stock is credited, and a PATCH of `stock` settles it against the count you send). stock and backordered are never both positive: a product at stock 0 with backordered 3 is three units in debt, which an admin UI presents as -3, and is a different thing from stock 0 with backordered 0, which is merely sold out.

backorder_notice.description: Operator-authored copy shown to shoppers while this product is flagged AND short of what they are asking for: on the product page once stock reaches 0, and in the cart whenever the line quantity exceeds the stock on hand (5 in stock with 10 in the cart is a backorder). null (the default) means the shopper is told NOTHING — a deliberate choice, never filled in with a default. Escaped server-side, like a payment method's instructions.

supplier_id.description: The supplier (GET /api/v1/suppliers) this product is bought from, or null. Must belong to this store on write (400 otherwise). Deleting the supplier sets this to null (ON DELETE SET NULL) rather than touching the product.

cost_price.description: OPERATOR-ONLY. Integer minor units, this product's own unit cost, or null for UNKNOWN (never zero — a known cost of nothing is a distinct claim). Snapshotted onto each order item's cost_snapshot at checkout; never rendered on any shopper-facing surface.

supplier_external_id.description: OPERATOR-ONLY. This product's own id in its supplier's namespace (an AliExpress item id when the supplier's provider is 'aliexpress'). On WRITE, accepts either the bare item id or a full AliExpress item URL and parses the id out of it; a value that names neither is a 400. Always rendered back, and always readable, as the bare id — never the URL that was sent. Requires the product to already carry a non-null supplier_id (400 otherwise). null means no external id is recorded. Never rendered on any shopper-facing surface. Setting this labels where the product comes from only, by itself — it is bookkeeping. POST /api/v1/suppliers/{supplierId}/sync (slice 6b-b) is the endpoint that actually pulls cost and stock from AliExpress for a product carrying this field; see supplier_stock below and the sync endpoint's own description for what it writes and what it never does.

supplier_stock.description: OPERATOR-ONLY, read-only (slice 6b-b). What the supplier LAST REPORTED as their own stock, written only by POST /api/v1/suppliers/{supplierId}/sync — never client-writable via POST/PATCH on this endpoint, and never touched by anything else. null until the first successful sync. This is NOT the store's sellable stock: it is informational only and a sync NEVER writes the `stock` field above — `stock` alone drives reservation, oversell and backorder logic. Never rendered on any shopper-facing surface.

supplier_synced_at.description: OPERATOR-ONLY, read-only (slice 6b-b). Unix timestamp of this product's last successful sync from POST /api/v1/suppliers/{supplierId}/sync, or null if it has never synced. Never client-writable. A sync only ever happens when that endpoint is called — nothing on this platform schedules one automatically.

parent_id.description: Set on a VARIANT row: the product it belongs to. Listings return parents only unless ?include_variants=1.

options.description: On a variant row: its option values as a JSON object string.

variant_count.description: List rows only: how many variants the product has.

category_ids.description: List rows only: the product's category ids.

primary_category_id.description: The category the storefront breadcrumb shows for this product; always one of its categories. null = the first category by sort order is used.

custom_fields.description: Product detail fields, key → value. Keys follow the categories' field_presets (inherited down the tree); any other key is an ad-hoc field shown with a humanized label. Single-product GET only.

tags.description: Tag names on the product (list rows and the single read).

tax_class_id.description: Tax engine T1 (migration 0210): one of this store's tax classes (GET /api/v1/tax/classes); null = the `standard` class. A variant with no class inherits its parent's. Absent (reads null) on a tenant that predates the column.

StoreOrder.description: A store order (slice 3a: read-only; status transitions arrive in a later release). Money fields are integer minor units in the order's own currency — totals are what was charged at checkout and are never re-derived from live product rows. The tax fields (tax_amount, tax_rate_bp, tax_inclusive) and the shipping fields (shipping_amount, shipping_label and the six shipping_* address fields) are SNAPSHOTS of what the order was charged, what the delivery line was called, and where the parcel goes — never the store's current tax or shipping settings, and never a customer's current saved address. shipping_method_id rides alongside them as an operator-reporting REFERENCE to the method chosen (slice 5b-b) — nothing shopper-facing reads it, and it goes null if that method is later deleted while the label and amount stay put. customer_id and customer_email are null for guest orders; email/name are the contact details captured on the order itself at checkout; phone is copied from the shopper's account at checkout time — guest checkout collects no phone, so it is null on guest orders.

customer_id.description: Null for guest checkout, or when the customer account was later deleted.

customer_email.description: The linked customer account's current email; null for guest orders.

email.description: Contact email captured on the order at checkout.

awaiting_gateway.description: 1 exactly when the order is pending_payment AND an online-provider payment attempt (payplus, hyp) is still pending — the shopper was handed to the gateway and no result has come back (typically an abandoned checkout), and the order holds any tracked stock it decremented until it is paid or cancelled. 0 for offline pending_payment orders (waiting on a human, e.g. a bank transfer that has not arrived) and for every order the gateway already answered. There is no automatic expiry in this release — filter ?status=pending_payment and check this flag to find orders holding stock for an abandoned online payment.

total.description: Integer minor units. What was actually charged, and what the payment row books — never recomputed from live prices or current settings. It is subtotal + shipping_amount + tax_amount when tax_inclusive is 0, and subtotal + shipping_amount when it is 1 (an inclusive order's tax is already inside subtotal). Deriving tax as total - subtotal is therefore WRONG on any shipped order — read tax_amount and shipping_amount.

tax_amount.description: Integer minor units of tax on this order, SNAPSHOTTED at checkout. Never recomputed from the store's current tax settings: changing the rate must not rewrite an issued receipt. 0 on an untaxed order, and absent entirely on orders placed before the tax columns existed.

tax_rate_bp.description: The tax rate this order was charged at, in BASIS POINTS (1700 = 17%, 825 = 8.25%) — the store's rate at checkout time, snapshotted alongside the amount. 0 when the order was not taxed.

tax_inclusive.description: The terms this order was taxed under. 0 = exclusive: the listed prices excluded tax, tax_amount was ADDED, and total is subtotal + tax_amount. 1 = inclusive: the listed prices already contained the tax, tax_amount was EXTRACTED out of subtotal for the record, and total equals subtotal. Displaying one as the other misstates what the customer paid.

shipping_amount.description: Integer minor units charged for delivery on this order, SNAPSHOTTED at checkout and included in total. Never recomputed from the store's current shipping settings: changing the rate must not rewrite an issued receipt. 0 on an order that was not shipped, and absent entirely on orders placed before the shipping columns existed.

shipping_label.description: What the delivery line was CALLED on the page the shopper agreed to — the chosen shipping method's name, or 'Shipping' when the store-level flat rate applied — snapshotted alongside the amount so renaming or deleting a method cannot blank the line on an order that used it. null when the order carries no delivery charge. This — not the amount — is what decides whether a shipping line is displayed: a store shipping free at a zero rate has a label and genuinely shows 'Shipping: 0.00'.

shipping_line1.description: Delivery address line 1, as the shopper gave it at checkout. Snapshotted on the ORDER: a customer editing their account later must not rewrite where a parcel already went. null when the order carries no address.

shipping_line2.description: Delivery address line 2 (apartment, floor). Optional at checkout, so null is ordinary.

shipping_city.description: Delivery city, as given at checkout.

shipping_region.description: Delivery state/region/province. Genuinely optional — many countries have none — so null is ordinary.

shipping_postcode.description: Delivery postal code, as given at checkout.

shipping_country.description: Delivery country as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, upper case ('IL', 'US'). Two letters exactly — a country name is rejected at checkout.

shipping_method_id.description: The shipping method (GET /api/v1/shipping-methods) the shopper chose, kept for OPERATOR REPORTING only — 'how many orders chose Express'. It is a reference, never the display: what to render is shipping_label, which is the name snapshotted at checkout. null on an order placed under the store-level flat rate, on an order with no delivery charge, and on any order whose method has since been deleted (ON DELETE SET NULL — the label and amount survive that deletion unchanged). Absent on orders read while the column has not been migrated yet; the rest of the shipping snapshot stays present through that window.

discount_total.description: Discounts v1: goods discount + waived shipping, integer minor units, snapshotted at checkout. 0 when nothing applied. total = subtotal − discount_total + shipping_amount (+ tax_amount when tax_inclusive is 0). shipping_amount stays the method's price even when a free-shipping entry waived it.

discounts.description: Discounts v1: what applied, snapshotted at checkout — [] when nothing did. An entry with shipping: true means the delivery charge was waived (amount = the waived price, already inside discount_total). Render this list; never recompute it. shipping: true entries may carry amount 0 when the delivery was already free; the shipping line shows the price struck with the remainder.

refundable_amount.description: Integer minor units still refundable on this order, DERIVED on every read: the settled (received) charge's amount minus the sum of the order's non-failed refund rows. A pending refund row is a reservation taken before the gateway is called and holds its amount; a failed row is a released reservation and holds nothing. 0 when nothing has been captured. Never stored, never accepted from a client — POST /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/refunds validates every refund against this same derivation.

margin.description: OPERATOR-ONLY, derived on every GET /api/v1/orders/{id} read — never stored, never accepted from a client. amount is the SUM of every costed item's margin and is null (never 0) when zero items have a cost_snapshot. costed and total are how many of the order's items had a cost snapshot versus how many items there are. partial is true whenever costed < total, meaning amount understates the order's true margin rather than fully stating it — report a partial figure as partial.

amount.description: Integer minor units, or null when costed is 0.

partial.description: true when costed < total — amount covers only some of the order's items.

costed.description: How many of the order's items carry a cost_snapshot.

total.description: How many items the order has.

sources.description: OPERATOR-ONLY, derived on every GET /api/v1/orders/{id} read — never stored, never accepted from a client. Keyed by product id AS A STRING (e.g. "42", never a numeric key). Each entry is {provider, external_id, url}: provider and external_id mirror the product's CURRENT supplier_id/supplier_external_id (a live fact, unlike the item's own purchase-time snapshot fields), and url is the AliExpress item link when provider is 'aliexpress' and external_id is set, else null. A line item's product is OMITTED from this object entirely — never present with null fields — when it has NO SUPPLIER AT ALL, or the product was deleted; the same omission applies during the migration window before the underlying columns exist. A product that HAS a supplier but no external id set yet is a different, real state (sourced, not yet linked) and IS present, as {provider, external_id: null, url: null} — omission means only 'no supplier', never 'no id'. `sources` itself is unaffected by whether a sync has ever run (slice 6b-b) — it only ever describes where a product is sourced FROM, never whether its cost/stock has been pulled from there; see StoreProduct.supplier_stock and StoreProduct.supplier_synced_at for that.

url.description: The AliExpress item link, or null for a manual supplier or a missing external id.

customer_type.description: Snapshotted at checkout (customer profile C1, migration 0193); individual on orders placed before it.

tax_treatment.description: What the tax engine decided (migration 0194). reverse_charge needs a business customer with a valid eu_vat ID in a different EU country than the store's origin_country; exempt is C2; not_taxable when the store has tax off. Never rewritten by later profile edits. Tax engine T1: an order the engine judged not_registered (tax_no_rule_fallback none, no jurisdiction row for the address) reads `not_taxable` here — the column's enum is fixed — and `tax_breakdown.treatment` says not_registered.

tax_jurisdiction.description: JSON {basis, country, region_code, id} — which address decided the taxable jurisdiction (migration 0195).

id.description: Tax engine T1: the store_tax_jurisdictions row that decided the rate, null on the flat fallback, under a zero-tax treatment, and on orders placed before migration 0204.

tax_id_snapshot.description: JSON {type, country, value, status} of the tax ID the treatment used — or the ID supplied even when treatment stayed standard (migration 0196). The FULL value: the receipt that used it must show it. null when none was given.

shipping_name.description: The address's recipient name, else the order name (migration 0187).

tax_breakdown.description: Tax engine T1 (migration 0215): the breakdown snapshot, parsed (GET /api/v1/orders and /api/v1/orders/:id) — {basis, country, region_code, jurisdiction_id, provider, mode: exclusive|fixed_gross|fixed_net, home_rate_bp, treatment, groups: [{class, rate_bp, goods, goods_tax, shipping, shipping_tax, shipping_taxed}], adjustment}. `treatment` is the engine's own word and is the only place `not_registered` (a `none` fallback with no rule for the address) appears — the tax_treatment column then reads not_taxable. TaxJar orders also carry `jurisdictions` (the provider's raw jurisdiction block). The three T1 keys are omitted (as every C1 key is) on tenants that predate the columns; null when the order predates them.

tax_provider.description: Who priced the order (migration 0216): the local engine, TaxJar, or the local engine standing in after a TaxJar failure (one audit_log row tax.provider.fallback). Omitted on tenants that predate the column.

tax_adjustment.description: Migration 0217, signed minor units: what the shopper paid for the goods and delivery below (+) or above (−) the listed prices — fixed_net pricing, or a zero-tax treatment on a tax-inclusive store. total = subtotal − discount_total − tax_adjustment + shipping_amount + (exclusive ? tax_amount : 0). Omitted on tenants that predate the column.

seller_registration_snapshot.description: Merchant registrations M1 (migration 0244): WHICH of the seller's own tax registrations this order was charged under, parsed (detail only — GET /api/v1/orders/:id; NOT carried on the GET /api/v1/orders list) — {id, kind, scheme, country, number}. NULL when none applied: every pre-M1 order, every order on a store that has declared no registrations, and every order whose destination resolved to none. On a reverse-charge order this is the ORIGIN registration (the number the reverse-charge sentence cites); otherwise it is the destination's. Omitted entirely on a tenant that predates the column.

StoreOrderItem.description: A line item, rendered from its purchase-time snapshot: name and unit_price are what was sold at what price, immune to later product edits. product_id is null when the product was deleted after the sale. cost_snapshot and margin are OPERATOR-ONLY and never appear on any shopper-facing surface. Tax engine T1 adds the per-line tax snapshot (tax_amount, tax_rate_bp, tax_class_slug, tax_jurisdiction_id) — read them, never recompute.

name.description: Name snapshot at purchase time.

unit_price.description: Integer minor units, snapshotted at purchase time.

discount_snapshot.description: Discounts v1: this line's share of the order's goods discount, integer minor units, snapshotted at checkout (largest-remainder allocation). 0 when none applied. line_total − discount_snapshot is what the shopper paid for the line.

cost_snapshot.description: OPERATOR-ONLY. The product's cost_price at the moment of sale, integer minor units, snapshotted — never a live join back to the product. null when the cost was unknown at sale time (or the product has since been deleted).

margin.description: OPERATOR-ONLY, derived: line_total - discount_snapshot - cost_snapshot * quantity. null (never 0) whenever cost_snapshot is null — an unknown cost yields an unknown margin, never a reported zero or full margin.

tax_amount.description: Tax engine T1 (migration 0211): this line's tax, integer minor units, snapshotted at checkout. 0 on a pre-T1 row and under zero-tax treatments.

tax_rate_bp.description: The rate this line was taxed at, basis points (migration 0212). 0 on a pre-T1 row.

tax_class_slug.description: The EFFECTIVE class the line resolved to (migration 0213) — `standard` when its own class had no rate in the jurisdiction. null on a pre-T1 row.

tax_jurisdiction_id.description: The jurisdiction row that priced the line (migration 0214); null under the flat fallback, TaxJar, zero-tax treatments, or on a pre-T1 row. No FK — the snapshot outlives the rule.

StorePaymentMethod.description: An operator-defined payment method. The operator owns the display text (name, instructions, enabled, sort_order); the provider identifier comes from a fixed registry. Deleting a method never destroys payment records — payments snapshot the provider and name at payment time.

provider.description: The fixed provider kind this method is backed by — what payment code dispatches on. payplus is implemented (redirect flow: the storefront checkout hands the shopper off to the PayPlus-hosted payment page). hyp is registered but NOT yet implemented: a method may be configured for it, but checkout refuses it as not yet available.

name.description: Operator-facing and shopper-facing display name, 1-120 characters (trimmed).

instructions.description: Free-text payment instructions shown to the shopper (e.g. bank details), at most 4000 characters, or null.

enabled.description: 0/1 (booleans accepted). Only enabled methods are offered at checkout.

StoreShippingZone.description: An operator-defined shipping zone (spec ZD1). Matched against a shopper address at checkout by country then region, most specific wins; a store with zero zones falls back to the flat shipping_flat_amount on Settings.

countries.description: Either the catch-all '*', or a comma-separated, upper-cased list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes (e.g. 'IL,CY').

regions.description: Comma-separated region/state names this zone is restricted to, or null for the whole country.

StoreShippingMethod.description: An operator-defined shipping method nested under a zone (spec ZD1/ZD7). price and free_over are integer minor units; a method is offered free when the cart subtotal is at or above free_over. Deleting the zone deletes the method with it; a past order keeps its own shipping_label/shipping_amount snapshot regardless.

free_over.description: Integer minor units, or null (never free by threshold).

country_rates.description: Phase H2 (migration 0096). JSON string mapping 2-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes to non-negative integer minor units, e.g. '{"IL":500,"US":1000,"JP":1500}', or null (no per-country overrides). On GET, returned as-is (JSON string). At checkout, pickMethod prefers the country-specific rate for the shopper's shipping_country; a country not in the map falls back to the method's base price. null / empty object / empty string = no overrides.

StoreSettings.description: The store's configuration: exactly these 38 fields, nothing else (id, slug and user_id are never exposed here). The tax fields (tax_enabled, tax_rate, tax_inclusive), the shipping fields (shipping_enabled, shipping_flat_amount, tax_shipping), emails_enabled and email_log_retention_days are LIVE: checkout applies the tax and shipping fields and snapshots the result onto the order, and — while emails_enabled is 1 — emails the shopper an order confirmation and, when the store has an email set, the operator a new-order alert; the same switch also sends the shopper a payment-confirmed email when the order reaches `paid` and a status email on every subsequent transition (processing, shipped, completed, cancelled, refunded). Slice 5c-c: emails_enabled alone is not enough — mail also requires a connected Brevo account (`PUT /api/v1/email-credentials`); a store without one sends nothing. Slice 5c-d adds a fifth mail kind, refund_confirmed, sent by a call that causes NO status transition: when a stranded refund reservation confirms and its confirmed total now completes coverage of the capture, it corrects a refunded figure that status_refunded quoted too low, sent at most once per order. email_log_retention_days (default 90, 0 = keep forever) controls how long store_email_log rows survive — checked once per send batch, but nothing is actually pruned until migration 0061 has run against a given tenant's database. The analytics ids (google_analytics_id, facebook_pixel_id) are STORED but not yet applied — they are emitted by the storefront in slice 6, so do not report them as live behaviour.

name.description: 1-60 characters.

tax_enabled.description: 0 or 1. LIVE: with 1, checkout taxes the order at tax_rate under the tax_inclusive terms and snapshots both onto it. With 0 no tax is charged and the order's tax fields are 0.

tax_rate.description: Percentage, 0-100. LIVE: the rate checkout charges at while tax_enabled is 1, snapshotted onto each order as tax_rate_bp (basis points).

tax_inclusive.description: 0 or 1. LIVE: 0 = the listed prices EXCLUDE tax and it is added on top (order total = subtotal + shipping + tax); 1 = the listed prices already CONTAIN it and the order records the tax extracted out of them (total = subtotal + shipping).

shipping_enabled.description: 0 or 1, default 0. LIVE: with 1, checkout collects a delivery address (line1, city, postcode and a 2-letter country are then REQUIRED — see POST /api/shop/checkout) and charges shipping_flat_amount, snapshotting both onto the order. With 0 no address is collected, no shipping line is shown anywhere, and orders record shipping_amount 0. Strictly 0 or 1 — true/false and '1' are a 400, unlike the tax flags.

shipping_flat_amount.description: Integer MINOR units (500 = 5.00), default 0, never negative. LIVE: the store-wide flat delivery charge applied while shipping_enabled is 1. A float is a 400, not rounded. 0 with shipping enabled is a real configuration — the store ships free and says so.

tax_shipping.description: 0 or 1, default 0. LIVE: whether the delivery charge is taxed. Tax is computed on ONE base with ONE rounding — subtotal + (tax_shipping ? shipping_amount : 0) — never on the goods and the delivery separately, which can differ by a minor unit. Strictly 0 or 1.

emails_enabled.description: Default 0. LIVE (slice 5c-a): while 1, a successful checkout emails the shopper an order confirmation and — when the store has an email address set — the operator a new-order alert. Slice 5c-b adds, to the same switch: a payment-confirmed email when the order reaches `paid` (by gateway callback or by the operator recording receipt), and a status email on every subsequent transition (`processing`, `shipped`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `refunded`). Each is sent once, by the call that actually caused the transition, and every attempt is recorded. Both render the ORDER's own snapshot, so a later settings change cannot rewrite a receipt that was already sent. Slice 5c-c: this toggle no longer implies a sender. Mail now requires a connected account (`PUT /api/v1/email-credentials`) and is sent from THAT account's own verified address and name — never a shared platform address. A store with this set to 1 but no connected account sends nothing; every attempt is still recorded, as `skipped` with `no_credentials`. A send that fails is likewise recorded and never affects the order.

google_analytics_id.description: Stored only in this release; emitted by the storefront in slice 6.

facebook_pixel_id.description: Stored only in this release; emitted by the storefront in slice 6.

gateway_mode.description: Which gateway credential rows checkout uses, store-wide: 'test' (default — a store that has not chosen cannot accidentally take live cards) or 'live'. Never selectable per request.

email_log_retention_days.description: Non-negative integer, default 90. STORED and validated live. Its PRUNING is not yet applied everywhere: checked once after every send batch to delete rows older than this many days, but nothing is pruned until migration 0061 has run against a given tenant's database — until then the column is simply absent there and no pruning happens. 0 means keep forever, not 'invalid' — a negative or fractional value is a 400. One row type is never pruned at any setting: a `sent` row of kind `refund_confirmed`, which is the guard that stops a duplicate refund-correction email to the shopper.

theme.description: Tenant customisation surface for the storefront token system (Phase G). Stored as a JSON TEXT column; read and written as an object. null or {} means default theme. Arrays and scalars are refused — the renderer expects an object. If rawCss is present, it is validated at save time (not just at render time). Serialised size is capped at 4000 bytes. Keys: palette (brand, brandHover, brandContrast, accent, accentContrast, accentBg, bg, surface, surfaceSubtle, text, textSecondary, textMuted, border, borderStrong, disabled, focus, success, successBg, danger, dangerBg, sale, warning, warningBg), geometry (radiusSm, radius, radiusLg), typography (fontSans, fontDisplay, sizeBody, sizeSmall, sizeH1, sizeH2, sizeH3), spacing (space, sectionY), layout (contentMax, contentReading), commerce (cardRatio), a nested dark object with the same vocabulary, and rawCss. Phase L1 choice keys, derived by the storefront: typeBase (15|16|17|18) + typeScale (1.125|1.2|1.25) → the size* tokens; spaceUnit (4|8|16) + density (compact|comfortable|spacious) → space/sectionY. Unknown keys are ignored at render time.

allow_split_checkout.description: 0 or 1, default 0. LIVE (Phase C, migration 0079): when 1, checkout shows a 'Pay in parts' toggle that lets the shopper split the order across multiple payments; when 0 the split-payment fieldset is not rendered. Strictly 0 or 1 — boolean coercion is not applied (same rule as shipping_enabled).

collects_shipping_address.description: 0 or 1, default 0. LIVE (Phase E, migration 0088): when 1, checkout collects a shipping (and optionally billing) address on every order that contains any physical product — even when shipping_enabled is 0. Turn off for digital-only stores where no delivery address is ever needed. Independent of shipping_enabled: a store shipping physical goods that do not need a delivery address (in-store pickup) can leave shipping_enabled off and this on. Strictly 0 or 1.

require_customer_account.description: 0 or 1, default 0. LIVE (Phase F, migration 0092): when 1, /checkout requires an authenticated shopper session; guest checkout returns a chooser page instead. When 0, /account/checkout-signin still renders as a chooser between sign-in and continue-as-guest. Strictly 0 or 1.

postal_code_required.description: 0 or 1, default 1. LIVE (Phase H, migration 0093): when 0, the shipping_postcode field's required attribute is dropped on the checkout SSR form AND the checkout API accepts an empty shipping_postcode. For markets without postcodes (Ireland outside D6W, parts of the Caribbean and Gulf). Strictly 0 or 1.

international_shipping.description: 0 or 1, default 1. LIVE (Phase H, migration 0094): when 1, checkout renders a country selector (populated from configured shipping zones when set, otherwise a curated 40-country common list plus an 'Other — enter code' fallback). When 0, the country selector is hidden and shipping_country is auto-filled with default_country (which must then be set). For single-country stores. Strictly 0 or 1.

default_country.description: 2-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (upper-cased) or null. Only load-bearing when international_shipping = 0. When set, orders placed on a single-country store record this as shipping_country regardless of shopper input (there is no input field to override it). A bad code is rejected at write time (not at checkout time). Phase H, migration 0095.

trust_strip_line_1.description: Plain-text trust-strip line shown on the product page (PDP redesign, migration 0121). At most 120 characters after normalisation; newlines and tabs collapse to a single space; empty or whitespace-only clears to null.

trust_strip_line_2.description: Second trust-strip line; same rules as trust_strip_line_1 (migration 0122).

shipping_policy_html.description: Shipping policy body shown on the product page (migration 0123). Sanitized at WRITE time to a fixed allowlist — p, br, strong, em, ul, ol, li, a[href] (http, https, mailto or relative) — every other tag is dropped and its text kept; GET returns the sanitized value. At most 4000 characters after sanitization (a 400 otherwise); empty clears to null.

returns_policy_html.description: Returns policy body; same rules as shipping_policy_html (migration 0124).

privacy_policy_html.description: The operator's own privacy policy prose (P10 task 1, migration 0279). This codebase does not generate a privacy policy — the operator writes it, and the public /privacy page publishes a system-generated factual section (cookies, their real lifetimes, and a visitor's resolved rights) beneath it whether or not this field is set. Sanitized at WRITE time to a WIDER allowlist than shipping_policy_html/returns_policy_html — the 'article' profile: p, br, strong, em, ul, ol, li, a[href], plus h2, h3, h4, blockquote, img[src,alt] — because a policy needs headings and is not a paragraph; every other tag is dropped and its text kept. At most 40000 characters after sanitization (a 400 otherwise, and the column is left unchanged); empty clears to null.

allow_business_customers.description: 0 or 1, default 1 (customer profile C1, migration 0198). When 0 the storefront hides the business option: a shopper profile PATCH / business save answers 403 business_customers_disabled and a checkout with customer_type business answers 400 business_customers_disabled (the checkout keeps the 400 family every other checkout validation uses; the profile endpoints use 403 because the action is forbidden store-wide, not malformed). Operators may still set customer_type through PATCH /api/v1/customers/{id}. Strictly 0 or 1.

require_company_for_business.description: 0 or 1, default 1 (migration 0199). When 1 a business checkout without a company is 400 company_required. Strictly 0 or 1.

require_phone_at_checkout.description: 0 or 1, default 0 (migration 0200). When 1 a checkout without a phone is 400 phone_required. Strictly 0 or 1.

tax_id_verification.description: Default vies (migration 0201). vies: an eu_vat ID is checked against the EU VIES REST API (4 s timeout; an outage yields status unavailable, never a failure); every other type is format-checked only. format_only: nothing leaves the worker — every ID that passes its format check lands as unverified.

tax_address_basis.description: Default shipping (migration 0202). Which address decides the taxable jurisdiction at checkout; falls back to the other when the chosen one is absent.

origin_country.description: 2-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (upper-cased) or null (migration 0203). The store's own tax country. Reverse charge needs it: a business customer with a valid eu_vat ID in a DIFFERENT EU country than this one pays 0 tax with tax_treatment reverse_charge. Null disables reverse charge.

tax_provider.description: Tax engine T1 (migration 0218): who prices a standard-treatment order — the local rules engine, or TaxJar (needs the token from PUT /api/v1/tax/provider-credentials for the store's gateway_mode, origin_country, and for a US origin origin_region_code + origin_postcode; exclusive pricing only — PATCH refuses `taxjar` while tax_inclusive is 1, and tax_inclusive 1 while the provider is taxjar, with 400 `tax_provider taxjar requires exclusive pricing`). Zero-tax treatments never reach the provider; any provider failure ends in the local result as tax_provider local_fallback with a tax.provider.fallback audit row.

tax_no_rule_fallback.description: Migration 0219: what happens when no enabled jurisdiction row matches the taxable address — flat: the legacy tax_rate / tax_shipping stand in as the home rule (today's behaviour); none: the order is not registered, no tax (tax_breakdown.treatment not_registered, tax_treatment not_taxable).

tax_inclusive_mode.description: Migration 0220, inclusive stores only (tax_inclusive 1): fixed_gross keeps the listed gross price and extracts the destination rate from it; fixed_net keeps the net (list price less the home rate — the Home jurisdiction's rate for the line's class, else the legacy tax_rate) and adds the destination rate on top — the difference is recorded as tax_adjustment on the order.

origin_region_code.description: Migration 0221: the ISO 3166-2 subdivision of origin_country the store ships from (TaxJar from_state; required for a US origin). Written as "TX", "US-TX" or "Texas" and resolved against origin_country's list — a region for a country with no list, an unknown region, or a region without an origin_country is a 400; changing origin_country to one the stored region does not belong to clears it.

origin_postcode.description: Migration 0222: the origin postal code (TaxJar from_zip; required for a US origin). Trimmed; empty clears to null.

require_email_verification.description: 0 or 1, default 0. LIVE (account integrity A1, migration 0237): when 1, shoppers who registered after the switch was turned on must verify their email address before member checkout, tax-ID add, business-profile save and exemption submit (403 email_unverified); guest checkout is untouched and accounts created before the switch are never gated. Turning it on stamps email_verification_since once; turning it off clears nothing. Strictly 0 or 1.

email_verification_since.description: A1 (1.24.0, migration 0238): unix seconds when require_email_verification was first turned on; null until then. Accounts created before this stamp are never gated. Read-only — PATCH refuses it (400 unknown_field:email_verification_since); it is stamped by PATCH { require_email_verification: 1 } and never cleared.

tracking_enabled.description: 0 or 1, default 0 — the operator's tracking master switch (P7, migration 0274). While 0 the storefront loads NO analytics or advertising script, whatever google_analytics_id or facebook_pixel_id hold; the column arrives as 0 for every store, so an upgrade can never turn tracking on. It gates entries whose category is not strictly_necessary, and it is only one of two conditions: a shopper's own consent verdict still decides whether a permitted script actually fires. Strictly 0 or 1 — a boolean or a string such as "yes" is a 400, never a coerced 1.

consent_retention_days.description: Days to keep privacy_consent_records rows (P7, migration 0276). NULL — the default on every store, and the value a pre-0276 tenant reads back — means NEVER SWEEP: no record is ever deleted. There is no default number and none is suggested: the rule that would carry one, eprivacy.consent_state.retention_period, is the only row in the pack with an empty source_url (confidence UNVERIFIED, encode: false) because CNIL recommandation 2020-092 was never fetched — the six months widely reported was not read from the document. A positive integer or null; "180", 0, 1.5 and true are 400s, never coerced. The sweep it drives is keyed on created_at, NEVER on expires_at (validity is a different, shorter clock than the proof obligation in GDPR Art. 7(1)), is bounded to 10 rows per shopper write, and never deletes a subject's most recent record nor a withdrawal that is their current answer.

id.description: null when the owner has no cart yet.

subtotal.description: Integer minor units (1999 = 19.99). Sum of available lines only.

discounts.description: Discounts v1: the cart's codes re-evaluated against the live lines on EVERY read (never stored) — a code that stopped qualifying surfaces in `rejected` with its reason. Delivery is unknown on the cart, so country-conditioned codes are `pending` and a free_shipping entry carries amount 0 until checkout prices the method.

pending.description: true when only a delivery address is missing — keep the code, do not show it as an error.

goods.description: Total taken off the goods lines, integer minor units.

delivery_dependent.description: true when a live discount depends on the delivery address or option — the checkout page re-prices with the chosen delivery.

codes.description: The codes remembered on the cart (max 3), uppercase.

price.description: The LIVE product price in integer minor units — a cart re-reads the catalogue; only a placed order snapshots prices (CD6). Deliberately not named unit_price: that name is the add-time snapshot column, which this field does not mirror.

available.description: false when the line cannot be sold as-is — product archived, hidden, re-listed in a currency other than the cart's, or priced past the money ceiling. The line stays visible but is excluded from subtotal.

backorder_notice.description: The operator's backorder notice for this line, or null. Non-null ONLY when the product allows oversell AND is out of stock; null also when the operator deliberately left the notice empty, which the storefront renders as saying nothing at all.

discount.description: This line's share of discounts.goods, integer minor units (0 when none).

tax_class_slug.description: Tax engine T1: the line's tax class slug (the product's store_tax_classes row, a variant inheriting its parent's), 'standard' when the product has none or the tenant predates migration 0204.

StoreCustomer.description: A shopper account, as the operator sees it. Deliberately partial: password_hash never crosses the API. Customer profile C1 (spec 1.21.0) adds phone, email_verified_at, customer_type, tax_status and company to the list rows; the full profile, business identity, tax IDs and address book are on GET /api/v1/customers/{id}. C2 (1.23.0) adds tags and pending_exemptions. A1 (1.24.0) adds deletion_requested_at (email_verified_at was already there).

status.description: A disabled shopper cannot log in, and every live storefront session dies the moment the account is disabled — re-enabling does not revive old sessions.

phone.description: The account's live phone (E.164 when it was normalised at registration). Orders still carry the phone captured at checkout.

email_verified_at.description: Unix seconds when the shopper proved the address; null until then. Reads null on a tenant that has not run migration 0176.

customer_type.description: From the profile row; individual when the shopper has no profile yet.

tax_status.description: The BEST status across the customer's tax IDs, ranked valid > manual_review > unavailable > unverified > invalid; none when the customer has no tax ID (a verifying row reads as unverified).

company.description: The business profile's legal_name, null when there is none.

tags.description: Operator-only customer tags (C2 D7, spec 1.23.0), by name; [] on a tenant still finishing migration 0230.

pending_exemptions.description: COUNT of this customer's tax exemptions awaiting review (C2, spec 1.23.0); 0 pre-0227.

deletion_requested_at.description: A1 (1.24.0): unix seconds of a pending deletion request, null when none (and on tenants before migration 0235).

gated.description: A1 (1.24.0): true when the store's require_email_verification switch is on, was stamped before this account was created, and the address is unverified — the same rule as CustomerDetail.gated, evaluated once per request against the store's settings. Always false on tenants before migration 0237. The admin's Unverified badge reads this, not email_verified_at.

EmailLogEntry.description: One row of this store's mailer activity, from GET /api/v1/email-log. `message_id` (Brevo's own id for a sent message) is deliberately never included in this or any response — it identifies a message to Brevo support and answers no question an operator has here.

kind.description: order_confirmation, operator_new_order, payment_confirmed, refund_confirmed, or status_<status> for the status the order transitioned to (status_processing, status_shipped, status_completed, status_cancelled, status_refunded).

error.description: Set on failed (e.g. brevo_500) and skipped (e.g. no_credentials, no_recipient, no_from_address, already_sent) rows; null on sent.

AuditLogEntry.description: One audit_log row, from GET /api/v1/audit-log on a STORE tenant. `details` is whatever the writer recorded, already parsed from the stored JSON text — an object, or null when nothing was recorded or the stored text is not valid JSON. The PAT writers record `{name, readOnly, expiresAt, prefix}` on create and `{revokedByAdmin}` on delete; the raw token and its hash never appear here.

id.description: Monotonic (AUTOINCREMENT): id order is time order. The paging cursor.

action.description: e.g. create, delete. Only the PAT lifecycle is audited in this release.

Supplier.description: A store supplier (slice 6a, extended in slice 6b-a; credentials and sync added in slice 6b-b) — who this store buys from. provider names which adapter namespace the supplier's ids live in ('manual' or 'aliexpress'); see StoreProduct.supplier_external_id and StoreOrder.sources for the rest of what 6b-a added, and the /api/v1/suppliers/{supplierId}/credentials, /verify and /sync endpoints below for what 6b-b added. This object never carries the stored credential itself (app_secret/access_token) — that lives only behind the credentials endpoint, and even its own GET never returns those two fields.

provider.description: Which adapter namespace this supplier's ids live in. Defaults to 'manual' on create. A 'manual' supplier has no adapter at all — the credentials, verify and sync endpoints below all refuse it with 400 supplier_has_no_adapter. Setting 'aliexpress' by itself still only labels where products from this supplier come from; see the credentials/verify/sync endpoints for the part that actually talks to AliExpress.

delta_pct.description: vs. the equal-length prior period; null when that prior period was 0 (never divide by zero).

type_slug.description: Unique identifier for the block type (e.g., 'heading', 'image', 'product-grid')

display_name.description: Human-readable name for the block editor UI

schema.description: JSON Schema for the block's config validation

default_config.description: Default configuration when a block of this type is first created

preview_svg.description: SVG representation for the block picker preview

is_seedable.description: Whether this block type can be seeded into templates

requires_context.description: If set, this block can only render in certain template contexts (render-time validation only, not stored)

sort_order.description: Display order in the block palette

schema.description: JSON Schema for the block type

counts.description: Count of templates by type (home, product-detail, category, all-products, custom)

slug.description: Must be unique across templates (409 on duplicate)

expires_at.description: Unix epoch seconds when the token expires

PatchTemplateRequest.description: All fields optional; submit only the parts you want to change

custom_css.description: Store product only. Template-level custom CSS; null or "" clears it. 400 `template_custom_css: <reason>` on @import, url() that is not a data: URI, expression(), `</style>`, non-printable bytes or >8000 bytes. Block `config.custom_css` is checked the same way: 400 `invalid_block_config:<slug>:custom_css: <reason>`.

zones.description: New or updated zones. Each { id?, slug, name, order_index, description?, max_blocks? }

draft.description: Draft blocks. Each { id?, block_type, zone_slug, order_index, config, status? }

published.description: Published blocks (read-only in response, ignored in PATCH)

customer_id.description: The signed-in shopper who wrote it, null for a guest.

FormSubmission.description: A contact-form submission (store_form_submissions, store-forms-p2 Tasks 1/6/8/9). `fields`/`values` are populated only by GET /api/v1/form-submissions/{id}, never by the list.

read_at.description: Unix seconds, stamped the first time status becomes 'read'. Null until then.

notified_at.description: Unix seconds the store owner was successfully emailed. Null when mail was never configured or every send attempt failed (Task 8) — the inbox surfaces this.

fields.description: GET /{id} only. The field DEFINITIONS as they were at submit time (fields_snapshot), parsed — never the live block config, so a submission still labels correctly after its form is edited.

values.description: GET /{id} only. The submitted values (values_json), parsed and keyed by field key.

excerpt.description: Operator-set, or derived from body_html when blank — see utils/posts.js's deriveExcerpt.

meta_description.description: Operator-set, or falls back to the excerpt when blank.

social_image_url.description: Operator-set, or falls back to the body's first when blank.

published_at.description: Unix seconds, stamped on the FIRST transition into published and never moved after that. Null for a post that has never been published.

ProductVariant.description: A variant is a product row of its own (parent_id = the product): its own price, compare_at_price, stock and oversell flag, sold under the parent's name and images. Name and slug are derived: "<parent name> — <values joined by ' / '>".

options.description: The option names, in display order.

CategoryRules.description: Smart-category rules. When set, membership is AUTOMATIC: the category's products are exactly those matching the conditions, re-derived when the rules are saved and re-checked for a product every time it is created or edited. null = manual membership. Money values are integer minor units.

op.description: name: contains|not_contains|starts_with|ends_with|equals. price/compare_at_price/stock: gt|gte|lt|lte|eq. featured/on_sale: eq. product_type/status/supplier_id: eq|ne. created_days_ago: lte (added within the last N days) | gt (older than N days). tag: has|not_has (matched by slug).

value.description: string for name; non-negative integer for price/compare_at_price/stock/supplier_id/created_days_ago; boolean for featured/on_sale; the enum value for product_type/status.

CategoryProduct.description: A product as listed inside one category.

position.description: The product's place in THIS category's storefront order (store_product_categories.sort_order).

is_primary.description: 1 when this is the product's primary category (the one its breadcrumb shows).

category_count.description: How many categories the product is in altogether.

smart.description: true when the category's membership is rule-driven.

FieldPreset.description: One product detail field a category asks its products for. `key` derives from the label (a-z, 0-9, _) unless given; it is the key in the product's custom_fields.

unit.description: number only: printed after the value (6.1 in).

required.description: The admin refuses to publish (status active) a product missing it; the API itself does not enforce it.

storefront.description: false keeps the value operator-only (not in the PDP's Specifications).

DiscountScope.description: What a discount applies to. order = every available line. products/categories carry ids (categories also include_children, default true — descendants count). tags carries slugs. Lines outside the scope are untouched; a code whose scope matches nothing in the cart is rejected (`doesn't apply to anything in your cart`).

DiscountConditions.description: Eligibility rules, all optional; {} = anyone, always. Money in integer minor units. Caps (per_customer_limit by email, total_limit against usage_count) are enforced again at checkout inside the order write, so a code can never be over-redeemed by two carts racing.

min_subtotal.description: Minimum eligible (in-scope) subtotal in minor units.

countries.description: ISO-2 delivery countries; until the shopper enters an address the code is `pending`, not rejected.

shipping_methods.description: ids of this store's shipping methods; the discount is pending until the shopper chooses a delivery option and rejected for any other option; accepted on every kind

total_limit.description: Redemptions allowed in total (compared with usage_count).

StoreDiscount.description: A discount as the operator API returns it: scope and conditions parsed (stored as JSON), usage_count maintained by checkout, redemption_count derived from the redemptions table. reward is the parsed Buy X get Y deal for kind bxgy, null otherwise.

code.description: Uppercase; null for an automatic discount.

kind.description: delivery discounts are percent/fixed rows with applies_to: shipping.

value.description: Basis points for percent, minor units for fixed, 0 for free_shipping and bxgy.

applies_to.description: shipping: a percent/fixed discount taken off the charged delivery price (capped at it); refused on bxgy and free_shipping

status.description: Only `active` is ever evaluated. Scheduled / expired are derived by the reader from starts_at / ends_at against now.

redemption_count.description: Rows in the redemptions table for this discount (what GET /discounts/{id}/redemptions lists).

amount.description: What this discount took off that order, integer minor units.

DiscountReward.description: The Buy X get Y deal (kind bxgy). buy names what the shopper must have in the cart, get names what is rewarded. Rewards are the CHEAPEST un-rewarded units in get.scope, one unit at a time. Same-scope rule: when buy.scope and get.scope are the same, a unit is either bought or rewarded, never both (buy 2 get 1 needs 3 units in the cart). repeats: true (default) rewards every full set the cart holds; max_rewards caps the total rewarded units. The discount row itself has value 0 and scope {type: order} — the reward carries both scopes.

buy.description: Exactly one of quantity or spend.

quantity.description: Units of buy.scope per set (quantity mode).

spend.description: Minor units spent on buy.scope per set (spend mode); in the same-scope case the spend is judged on the units left after the rewards are removed.

percent.description: Basis points taken off each rewarded unit (10000 = free).

repeats.description: Default true: every full set in the cart is rewarded. false: one set only.

max_rewards.description: Cap on rewarded units across all sets.

CustomerProfile.description: The per-customer profile row (migration 0177). Every field has a default, so a customer who never touched their profile still reads as a complete object; the operator detail returns null instead on a tenant that has not run 0177.

business_verification.description: Never moves DOWN automatically: saving a business profile makes an unverified customer self_declared; a tax ID reaching valid makes them tax_id_verified; an operator PATCH may set manually_verified or return them to self_declared; document_verified is reserved for C2.

default_billing_address_id.description: The default BILLING address is a profile field; is_default on an address still means default shipping.

operator_notes.description: Operator-only free text (≤ 4000 characters). Never returned to the shopper.

CustomerBusinessProfile.description: The customer's business identity (migration 0179), one row per customer; null on the detail when none was saved.

address_id.description: The registered office, an id from the customer's own address book.

contact_phone.description: E.164 when country is set, else bounded text.

CustomerTaxId.description: A customer tax identifier as it appears in every LIST response and on the customer list/detail — the value is MASKED (CP11): first 4 characters, ••••, last 2 (values of 6 or fewer characters show only the first 2). Audit-log details carry the same masked form. The full value is only on GET /api/v1/customers/{id}/tax-ids/{tid}.

type.description: eu_vat (EU + XI VAT IDs, VIES-verifiable), gb_vat, au_abn (checksum), ca_bn, in_gstin (checksum), us_ein, il_company, nz_gst, ch_uid, other.

label.description: Human label for the type: VAT ID, VAT number, ABN, Business number, GSTIN, EIN, Company number, GST number, UID, Tax ID.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; the type must be applicable to it (400 invalid_tax_id otherwise).

status.description: Server-side only — never settable by the shopper. unverified = format passed, no provider check (non-EU types, or tax_id_verification = format_only); valid / invalid = the provider's verdict; unavailable = the provider could not answer (VIES outage or timeout) — the row is kept and retried, and it never blocks a save or a checkout; manual_review = an operator parked it.

provider.description: Who produced the status: format (format check only), vies (EU VIES REST), operator (a PATCH override).

verified_at.description: Unix seconds of the last time the ID reached valid; only ever moves on valid.

CustomerTaxIdFull.description: A customer tax identifier with its FULL normalised value — returned only by the single-resource GET.

type.description: eu_vat (EU + XI VAT IDs, VIES-verifiable), gb_vat, au_abn (checksum), ca_bn, in_gstin (checksum), us_ein, il_company, nz_gst, ch_uid, other.

label.description: Human label for the type: VAT ID, VAT number, ABN, Business number, GSTIN, EIN, Company number, GST number, UID, Tax ID.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; the type must be applicable to it (400 invalid_tax_id otherwise).

value.description: The full normalised value (upper case, no spaces or punctuation), e.g. DE123456789.

status.description: Server-side only — never settable by the shopper. unverified = format passed, no provider check (non-EU types, or tax_id_verification = format_only); valid / invalid = the provider's verdict; unavailable = the provider could not answer (VIES outage or timeout) — the row is kept and retried, and it never blocks a save or a checkout; manual_review = an operator parked it.

provider.description: Who produced the status: format (format check only), vies (EU VIES REST), operator (a PATCH override).

verified_at.description: Unix seconds of the last time the ID reached valid; only ever moves on valid.

CustomerAddress.description: One entry of the shopper's address book, as the operator reads it. is_default marks the default SHIPPING address; the default billing address is CustomerProfile.default_billing_address_id. name/company/phone/region_code/kind are customer profile C1 (migrations 0182-0186) and read null / "both" on rows saved before them.

region.description: State/province name; overwritten with the subdivision name when region_code is given.

region_code.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code (the tax jurisdiction). Required for US, CA, AU, BR, IN, MX.

postcode.description: Empty string when the store has postal_code_required = 0.

name.description: Recipient name.

phone.description: E.164, normalised with the address country.

kind.description: Which checkout slot the address may fill.

CustomerDetail.description: One shopper, in full: identity, profile, business identity, MASKED tax IDs, address book and lifetime order figures. A1 (spec 1.24.0) adds pending_email, deletion_requested_at and gated.

profile.description: null ONLY on a tenant that has not run migration 0177 (upgrade window); a customer without a profile row reads the defaults.

addresses.description: Default shipping address first, then by id.

orders_count.description: COUNT of this customer's orders whose status is not cancelled, refunded or pending_payment.

total_spend.description: SUM(total), integer minor units, over the same orders (status not in cancelled, refunded, pending_payment). Money that did not stay, or never arrived, is not spend.

tags.description: Operator-only tags by name (C2 D7); null on tenants that predate the table (0230) — the admin hides the editor; [] means present and empty.

exemptions.description: Tax exemptions, newest first, with operator document URLs (C2); null on tenants that predate the table (0227) — the admin hides the card; [] means present and empty.

pending_email.description: A1 (1.24.0): the new address of an email change awaiting the shopper's confirmation; null when none (and on tenants before migration 0234).

deletion_requested_at.description: A1 (1.24.0): unix seconds when the shopper asked for deletion; the account is purged 14 days later unless cancelled (POST …/cancel-deletion, or the shopper signs in). null when none (and pre-0235).

gated.description: A1 (1.24.0): true when the store's require_email_verification switch is on, was stamped before this account was created, and the address is unverified — the shopper cannot place member orders or manage tax details until verified (POST …/verify lifts it). Always false on tenants before migration 0237.

TaxClass.description: Tax engine T1 (spec 1.22.0): a product tax class. Every store carries `standard` (the default when a product names no class, and the class a jurisdiction falls back to when it has no rate for the line's class) and `zero` (zero-rated; TaxJar category 99999 unless product_tax_code says otherwise). Both are protected: DELETE is 400 class_protected. Slugs are immutable (order items snapshot the slug).

product_tax_code.description: Provider category code (TaxJar product tax code) sent as product_tax_code on every line of this class; null = the provider's default.

TaxRate.description: One class's rate inside a jurisdiction. A jurisdiction with no rate for a line's class taxes it at its `standard` rate; a jurisdiction with no rates at all is registered at 0%.

applies_to_shipping.description: 1 = this class's proportional share of the delivery charge is taxed at this rate.

TaxJurisdiction.description: Tax engine T1: where the store is registered to collect tax — a whole country (region_code null) or one ISO 3166-2 subdivision of it. The taxable address (per the store's tax_address_basis) resolves to the most specific ENABLED row: region over country. No matching row → the store's tax_no_rule_fallback decides (flat = the legacy tax_rate as a synthetic home rule, none = not registered, no tax). (country, region_code) is unique per store (409 jurisdiction_exists).

country.description: 2-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, upper-cased on write; must be a known country.

region_code.description: ISO 3166-2 code (US-TX) or null for the whole country. Written as "TX", "US-TX" or "Texas" — resolved against the country's subdivision list; a country with no list only takes null.

enabled.description: Disabled rows are listed but never resolve.

rates.description: The rate set, ordered like the classes. Replaced wholesale with PUT /api/v1/tax/jurisdictions/{id}/rates.

Registration.description: Merchant registrations M1: the operator's own declaration that they are registered to collect tax somewhere — a registration AUTHORISES charging. For a taxable destination the engine resolves, in order: an active `country` row for the destination's country; else, when the destination is another EU member state, the active `oss` row; else none — and with NO registration the destination's jurisdiction rule is IGNORED and the order takes tax_no_rule_fallback (flat = the home rate, none = treatment not_registered at 0). Two rules keep existing stores unchanged: a store with ZERO rows charges exactly as it did before (the gate is skipped entirely), and the store's own origin_country is always treated as registered. The gate is applied BEFORE any external provider, so an unregistered destination never reaches TaxJar. Registrations are DECLARED, never inferred — there are no thresholds. Effective dating is EVALUATED, never enforced: a row outside its window is kept, listed and flagged active:false, and the engine ignores it. A country may therefore be registered for SUCCESSIVE periods — valid_to is exclusive, so a row closing where the next opens is accepted; only OVERLAPPING windows for one country are refused (409 registration_exists), as is a second OSS row.

kind.description: country = a registration in one country. oss = the EU One-Stop-Shop, whose `country` is the member state of identification. Immutable after creation (PATCH answers 400 unknown_field:kind).

scheme.description: A tax-ID type key from the same registry customer tax IDs use — eu_vat, gb_vat, au_abn, ca_bn, in_gstin, us_ein, il_company, nz_gst, ch_uid, other. The number is validated by that scheme's format rules for `country`. Note the keys: it is au_abn / in_gstin / nz_gst, never abn / gstin / gst.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, any case, upper-cased on write. For kind=oss it must be an EU VAT-area member state.

number.description: The registration number in full — NOT masked. These are the merchant's own numbers, not customer PII.

valid_from.description: Unix seconds, inclusive; null = always has been.

valid_to.description: Unix seconds, EXCLUSIVE; null = still current.

active.description: Whether the row is inside its window right now (valid_from <= now < valid_to). Derived on every read, never stored.

TaxPreviewRequest.description: A dry run of the tax engine: what an order to this address would be charged under the store's current rules, classes, settings and provider. Nothing is written, nothing is audited, and a TaxJar failure quotes local as `local_fallback` without an audit row.

region_code.description: Subdivision of the country ("CA", "US-CA", "California"); null for none.

address.description: Stands for both the shipping and the billing address, so either tax_address_basis resolves it.

amount.description: Integer minor units, the line total net of discounts.

tax_class_id.description: One of this store's classes (400 invalid_tax_class otherwise); null = standard.

shipping.description: The delivery charge, integer minor units.

tax_id_valid_country.description: Simulate a VALID eu_vat ID registered in this country on the customer — how reverse charge is previewed (business customer, EU origin, a different EU country).

exemption_country.description: Simulate an APPROVED tax exemption certificate for this country on the customer — how `exempt` is previewed. An exemption beats reverse charge; the address must be in this country (and region, when given) for it to apply.

exemption_region_code.description: Narrow the simulated exemption to one subdivision of exemption_country (ISO 3166-2, e.g. US-TX; a bare code or name resolves). 400 for a country with no region list, or a code of another country.

TaxPreviewResponse.description: The engine's result — the same figures checkout would snapshot. `provider` is who priced it (local | taxjar | local_fallback) and `fallback_reason` (null | unavailable | misconfigured | rejected) why TaxJar was not used. `treatment` is the engine's own word: standard | exempt | reverse_charge | not_registered | not_taxable (tax off). `lines[]` carry {id (1-based position), amount, charged, rateBp, classSlug (the EFFECTIVE class after fallback), jurisdictionId, tax}; `breakdown` is the same object GET /api/v1/orders/{id} returns as tax_breakdown; `adjustment` is the signed price adjustment an inclusive store would record.

bp.description: Display rate in basis points (blended when several rates apply).

total.description: What the shopper would pay: goods − adjustment + shipping + (exclusive tax).

id.description: The resolved jurisdiction row; null under the flat fallback, TaxJar, or no rule.

Exemption.description: A customer's tax exemption (C2, spec 1.23.0). `status` is what is stored; `effective_status` is what applies — an approved row past expires_at reads `expired` and the tax engine ignores it (no cron flips the row). An approved, unexpired exemption whose country (and region_code, when set) matches the order's taxable address makes the order `exempt` (tax 0; on an inclusive store the net is charged and tax_adjustment is owed) and beats reverse charge. `document` is null for an operator-vouched row created without a file; its `url` is the operator download route, never a public media URL.

expires_at.description: Unix seconds (00:00:00Z of the last valid date); null = no expiry.

url.description: Where the caller may download the file: the operator route (GET /api/v1/customers/{id}/exemptions/{eid}/document) on the operator API, the shopper's own download route on /api/shop/exemptions. Never a public media URL.

reviewed_by.description: The reviewing operator's email; null while pending.

StoreProductImage.description: One row of store_product_images. `source` is `upload` (three AVIF variants in the store's R2 bucket; thumb_url/medium_url/large_url are absolute URLs on STORE_R2_DOMAIN, present only when the tenant has that binding) or `url` (an external or relative URL stored verbatim; no R2 keys, no *_url fields). Exactly one image per product is primary; the first image attached becomes primary automatically.

format.description: `avif` for uploads, null for url rows.

file_size.description: Bytes of the large AVIF variant.

required.description: The role the route requires, e.g. "admin".

TemplateBundle.description: A portable export of templates and/or pages. Cross-entity references (category/tag/post/media ids) travel in each block's `refs` array rather than inside `config`, so `config` stays byte-exact and schema-valid; `refs` entries carry the slug/name/url an importer resolves against its own database.

theme.description: Recorded for forward compatibility only. NOT applied on import; this product has no per-tenant theme.

ref.description: Stable identifier other entries in this bundle use to point at this template (its export-time slug).

parent.description: `ref` of the parent (base layout) template in this same bundle, or null for a template that has no base layout. EXPORT ALWAYS EMITS THIS KEY: a ref string, or null. On an import that OVERWRITES an existing template, OMITTING the key preserves whatever parent the target already has, while an explicit null clears it - so a bundle that leaves it out is saying "I did not say", which is what a hand-written file usually means, and clearing the link there would strip the header and footer from a live design. On a CREATE, a missing key and null mean the same thing: no parent. The one case where an export omits the key is a template whose parent row could not be read; that is reported in the bundle's `anomalies` rather than guessed at as null.

included.description: `dependency` means this template was pulled in automatically as a parent (e.g. the base layout owning the header/footer), not requested directly.

config.description: Byte-exact, straight from this block's own stored config. Never rewritten on export - cross-entity ids stay local-id-shaped here; see `refs`.

refs.description: Portable identity for each cross-entity reference inside `config`, addressed by RFC 6901 JSON Pointer.

at.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into this block's `config`.

id.description: The exporting tenant's local id - meaningless on another site, carried only as a fallback.

templateRef.description: `ref` of this page's template in this bundle, if included.

content.description: Only present when exported with content=1.

anomalies.description: Present ONLY when the export could not state something faithfully, so a clean bundle does not carry the key at all. Today it has one member: a template whose `parent_template_id` names a row the export could not read, where `parent` is omitted rather than reported as null - omitting it means "preserve" on import, while null would falsely assert that the design has no base layout. The importer ignores this key.

template.description: slug of the template the anomaly is about

at.description: JSON Pointer to the field, e.g. "/parent"

TemplateImportPlan.description: What POST /api/templates/import/preview decided for a bundle. The same shape apply (Task 5) writes from - preview and apply share one decision engine so they can never disagree about what was about to happen. `valid: false` with HTTP 200 means the bundle is a well-formed report, not an attempt: at least one item needs a decision (an undecided slug collision), names something that does not exist (an unknown block type), or failed its own block schema.

valid.description: False if any error was recorded - an undecided collision, an unknown block type, or a block config that fails its own schema. A false plan can still be inspected; it cannot be applied.

action.description: 'collision' means the slug already exists and `onCollision` named no decision for it - the operator must choose create-new/overwrite/skip and preview again. A reserved slug is 'skip' with reason 'reserved_slug' and is NOT an error: the entry is left alone and the site's existing seeded row is used, including as the resolved `parent` of any child in the same bundle. There is no 'refused' action; a reserved slug used to produce one, which made every exported bundle unimportable because export auto-includes `default-base`.

assignedSlug.description: The slug apply would actually write - suffixed from -2 (not -1) when onCollision picked create-new.

reason.description: Why the action was decided for the caller rather than by them. 'reserved_slug' accompanies action 'skip': one of the eight seeded slugs (default-base, default-home, single-post, single-page, category-archive, tag-archive, search, default-404), which an import may never create or rename because control-plane migrations target them by name - any onCollision choice for such an entry is overridden. 'slug_exists' accompanies action 'collision'.

templateId.description: Present on action 'overwrite': the existing row apply will overwrite in place.

items.description: Only blocks that passed block-type and schema validation; a rejected block is dropped here and explained in `errors`.

config.description: Resolved to this site's own ids and with any rejected field (customCss, form-control attributes) already stripped - what apply will actually write.

unresolved.description: A category/tag/post reference this site has no matching slug for. Under the default onUnresolved:'fail' the import is refused and the field is left untouched; under 'drop' each entry carries `action` saying what was done with it.

at.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the block config.

action.description: Present only when the request set onUnresolved:'drop'. 'nulled' - the pointer was set to null, which that block's schema permits. 'block_skipped' - the schema has no null to write there, so the whole block was left out rather than stored with the exporting site's id.

externalMedia.description: A media reference whose file is not on this site. Importing it would hotlink another site's media rather than copy it, so it is reported instead of silently applied.
