rejected.description: A field the importer refused to pass through as-is, with what it did instead already applied to `templates[].zones[].blocks[].config`: 'css_rejected' (unsafe customCss, dropped), 'form_attrs_stripped' (action/formaction/method/name/value removed from a form-control tag in an imported HTML field, imported content being a different trust boundary than operator-authored content - see `removed`), 'html_sanitised' (the `html`/`content` field was run through the renderer's 'layout' allowlist, so script/iframe/style tags and every event-handler attribute are gone from what was stored) or 'unsafe_pointer' (a `refs[].at` JSON pointer naming __proto__/constructor/prototype; the reference was discarded, not merely unresolved). Entries for an imported PAGE body carry `page` instead of templateRef/zone/blockIndex, with at '/content' and reason 'html_sanitised'.

removed.description: Present on 'form_attrs_stripped': the attribute names actually removed.

theme.description: This product has no per-tenant theme to apply - `present` says whether the bundle carried one, `applied` is always false.

errors.description: Every reason `valid` is false: envelope defects, a parent cycle, an unknown block type, a block failing its own schema, or an undecided slug collision.

TemplateImportReport.description: What POST /api/templates/import/apply actually wrote, after the plan was valid and everything landed in one db.batch. A CREATED template or page lands status='draft', is_default=0, so it is inert until you publish it. An OVERWRITE is not inert: it replaces the target's zones and blocks in place and leaves status, is_default and the parent link as they were, so overwriting a published template or page changes what visitors see on the next request, and the CMS keeps no history to undo it.

created.description: Count of templates plus pages newly inserted.

overwritten.description: Count of templates plus pages whose existing row was overwritten (onCollision:'overwrite').

skipped.description: Count of templates plus pages left untouched (onCollision:'skip').

templates.description: Same per-template fields as TemplateImportPlan.templates, minus `zones` - this is a receipt, not the content.

pages.description: Same per-page fields as TemplateImportPlan.pages, minus `content`.

unresolved.description: Carried from the plan. Empty unless the request set onUnresolved:'drop', since the default ('fail') makes any unresolved reference a 400 instead of reaching this response. Each entry's `action` says whether the pointer was nulled or the block skipped.

theme.description: Carried from the plan - this product has no per-tenant theme to apply.

InvalidToken.description: Missing, invalid, expired, or revoked token.

ReadOnlyToken.description: Token is read-only; only GET/HEAD are permitted.

Forbidden.description:
Authenticated, but not authorized for this route. The route-policy gate in the shared API middleware answers before the handler runs, so the body is one of three codes:

- `insufficient_role` — the caller's role is below the route's minimum; `required` names it. Every /api/v1 route on a store tenant requires `admin`.
- `read_only_token` — a read-only PAT. Always on a write; and on the SIX reads where the read is itself the privileged act (`/customers/{id}/export`, `/customers/{id}/tax-ids/{tid}`, `/email-credentials`, `/gateway-credentials`, `/suppliers/{supplierId}/credentials`, `/tax/provider-credentials`). Those six GETs accepted a read-only token before spec 1.31.0; a cookie session is unaffected.
- `session_required` — the route may be read with a PAT but written only from a browser session (`/api-tokens`: a credential may not manage credentials).

get.description: Catalogue of the 20 block types this tenant can place in a template: `type`, `name`, `category` and `schemaUrl`. Public — no token required.

patch.description: Update a block instance; only the supplied fields change. Requires role editor or above; a lower-privileged token gets 403. `config` is MERGED into the stored config — incoming top-level keys overwrite or add to what is stored, and keys you omit are kept. This deliberately diverges from the GraphQL `updateBlockInstance` mutation, which REPLACES the whole config object. The merge is SHALLOW (top-level keys only): a nested object you pass replaces the entire stored nested object at that key. The merged result is re-validated against the block type's JSON Schema; a violation returns 400 with `validationErrors`.

400.description: Invalid block config: the merged/submitted config violates the block type's JSON Schema. Body carries `validationErrors`.

403.description: Requires the editor role or above. Read-only tokens and tokens for lower-privileged users are refused.

delete.description: Delete a block instance. Requires role editor or above; a lower-privileged token gets 403. Idempotent, matching zone deletes: an unknown id still returns 204, not 404.

204.description: Deleted (or already absent — deletes are idempotent)

403.description: Requires the editor role or above. Read-only tokens and tokens for lower-privileged users are refused.

get.description: The block type's JSON Schema with every `$ref` inlined, so it needs no second fetch. Every field the block accepts, its default and its `x-group` (the admin editor generates its form from this document). Config sent to `createBlockInstance` / `updateBlockInstance` is validated against it. Public — no token required. Answers 404 `unknown_block_type` for a type with no registered schema, which also means that type's config is stored unvalidated.
Read-only GraphQL: pass `query` and `variables` as query-string parameters. Mutations must use POST. Same schema as POST — see there for the Template/Zone/Block operations.

getTemplate.summary: Read one template with its zones and blocks

createZone.summary: Add a zone to a template

createBlockInstance.summary: Put a block in a zone (config follows the block's schema)

publishTemplate.summary: Publish a template, then assign it to a page

assignTemplateToPage.summary: Assign a template to a page

post.description:
Templates, Zones and Block instances are managed here — this endpoint is the write API for page structure. REST covers content (posts, pages, media, settings); the template tree is GraphQL.

Auth is identical to the REST endpoints: `Authorization: Bearer epat_...`. A read-only token gets 403 on any mutation, and every mutation additionally requires the `editor` role or higher — an `author`/`columnist`/`contributor` caller gets a `FORBIDDEN` GraphQL error (`editor role required`). Queries are unaffected. Reachable at both `/api/graphql` and `/api/v1/graphql` (same handler). GraphQL always answers 200 — check the `errors` array, not the status code.

**Queries**
- `templates(type: TemplateType, isBaseLayout: Boolean, limit: Int, offset: Int)`
- `template(id: ID, slug: String)` — includes `zones { blocks }`, `blocks`, `inheritedBlocks`
- `blockTypes(category: BlockCategory, isActive: Boolean)` / `blockType(type: String!)` — same catalogue as `GET /api/blocks` and `GET /api/blocks/{type}/schema`
- `themeTokens` — same payload as `GET /api/theme/tokens`
- Content reads, usable WITHOUT a token (the middleware allow-lists non-mutation documents naming them): `page`, `pages`, `post`, `posts`, `category`, `categories`, `tag`, `tags`, `search`, `searchSuggestions`, and the render previews `renderedHome`, `renderedPage`, `renderedPost`, `renderedPostArchive`, `renderedCategory`, `renderedTag` — the last group returns a template's blocks as the site would render them, which is how an agent checks its work without publishing a page

**Template mutations**
- `createTemplate(input: CreateTemplateInput!)` — `name`, `slug`, `type` (`PAGE|POST|ARCHIVE|HOME|ERROR|CUSTOM`), optional `description`, `isDefault`, `isBaseLayout`, `parentTemplateId`, `thumbnail`, `config`
- `updateTemplate(id, input: UpdateTemplateInput!)` — same fields, all optional, plus `status`
- `deleteTemplate(id)` → Boolean
- `publishTemplate(id)` / `revertTemplate(id)` — draft ⇄ published
- `setDefaultTemplate(id)` — makes it the default for its type
- `copyTemplate(id, input: { name, parentTemplateId })`
- `assignTemplateToPage(pageId, templateId)` / `assignTemplateToPost(postId, templateId)`

**Zone mutations**
- `createZone(input: { templateId!, name!, slug!, description, maxBlocks, orderIndex, config })`
- `updateZone(id, input: UpdateZoneInput!)`
- `deleteZone(id)` → Boolean
- `reorderZones(templateId, zoneIds: [ID!]!)` — array order becomes `orderIndex` 0..n

**Block-instance mutations**
- `createBlockInstance(input: { templateId, pageId, postId, zoneSlug!, blockType!, orderIndex, config!, visibility, isActive })` — the config is validated against that block's `GET /api/blocks/{type}/schema` — all 20 block types have one — and a violation is rejected with `extensions.code = "invalid_config"` plus a `validationErrors` array. Schema defaults are applied at render time, so the stored config is exactly what you sent
- `updateBlockInstance(id, input: UpdateBlockInstanceInput!)` — `config` REPLACES the stored object rather than merging into it, and is validated as a whole (so it must still carry the schema's `required` fields). Read the block, merge, send it back
- `deleteBlockInstance(id)` → Boolean
- `reorderBlockInstances(zoneSlug, blockIds: [ID!]!)` — reorders by id; note the returned list is every block sharing that zone slug, not only the current template's

**Typical agent flow:** `blockTypes` → `createTemplate` → `createZone` (per region) → `createBlockInstance` (per block, config from the block schema) → `reorderBlockInstances` → `publishTemplate` → `assignTemplateToPage`.

put.description: Assign (or replace) the template the page renders with; send `templateId: null` to unassign. Requires role editor or above; a lower-privileged token gets 403. Returns the updated page. 404 when the page or the template does not exist.

403.description: Requires the editor role or above. Read-only tokens and tokens for lower-privileged users are refused.

post.description: `theme_palette` (JSON object: primary, accent, text, background, muted, surface — each `#rrggbb`) and `theme_fonts` (JSON object: body, heading, mono — a self-hosted family name or `system`) are validated; an invalid value returns 400 `invalid_theme_setting`. An object value for either key is stored as its JSON string.

put.description: `theme_palette` (JSON object: primary, accent, text, background, muted, surface — each `#rrggbb`) and `theme_fonts` (JSON object: body, heading, mono — a self-hosted family name or `system`) are validated; an invalid value returns 400 `invalid_theme_setting`. An object value for either key is stored as its JSON string.

post.description: Add, edit, delete or set the default address in the signed-in shopper's OWN address book (slice 5b-c, AD9). Shopper-session authenticated only — there is no PAT-authenticated equivalent, because this is the shopper's own data and no operator surface reads it; an order snapshots its own address at checkout time and is never joined back to this table (AD1). Must be same-origin and echo __Host-shop_csrf in X-CSRF-Token, like every other shopper state change. One `action` field selects the operation, mirroring the account page's one-form-per-action shape: `add` (omit id) and `edit` (id required) validate line1, city, postcode and country as required and label/line2/region as optional, with the SAME normalisers checkout's shipping_address uses (AD8) — an address that saves cleanly here cannot then fail differently at checkout. `default` and `delete` take only id. Every write is scoped to this store AND the session's own customer_id — an id belonging to another customer or another store is 404 not_found, never touched, never revealing whether it exists elsewhere. The first address a customer saves becomes their default automatically; setting a new default clears the old one in the same transaction; deleting the default promotes the lowest remaining id (AD5). Editing or deleting an address never rewrites any past order's own address snapshot (AD1/AD6). Capped at 20 addresses per customer (400 too_many_addresses). Rate limited per IP.

parameters.name: X-CSRF-Token
parameters.description: The __Host-shop_csrf cookie value (HMAC-bound to this session).

action.description: default marks the default SHIPPING address (is_default); default_billing (customer profile C1) writes the profile's default_billing_address_id instead — 400 invalid_address for another customer's id, 503 unavailable before migration 0177.

id.description: Required for edit, delete and default; omitted for add. Scoped to this store and the session's own customer_id — any other id is 404 not_found.

label.description: The shopper's own word for the address ('Home', 'Office'). Optional.

postcode.description: May be omitted (stored as an empty string) when the store has postal_code_required = 0.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, case-insensitive on input and stored upper case.

name.description: Recipient name (C1).

region_code.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code; must be one of the country's subdivisions when it has a list, REQUIRED for US, CA, AU, BR, IN, MX (a `region` text naming the subdivision stands in for a missing code); region is overwritten with the subdivision name when given.

kind.description: Which checkout slot the address may fill. Default both.

200.description: add/edit return the address id; delete and default do not.

400.description: invalid_action (unrecognised action), invalid_address (a required field missing or hostile — control bytes, angle brackets, over length, or a country that is not exactly two ASCII letters), too_many_addresses (20-address cap), or an unknown field by name — client-supplied fields outside the allowlist are rejected, never ignored.

403.description: cross_origin_rejected (not same-origin) or CSRF token missing, mismatched, or bound to a different session.

404.description: not_found — id is not an integer, or does not resolve under this store and the session's own customer_id.

503.description: unavailable — store_customer_addresses does not exist yet (the migration upgrade window, AD7).

get.description: The shopper's business identity, null when none was saved (customer profile C1). Same session + CSRF belt as POST /api/shop/addresses: cookie __Host-shop_session, and on POST the __Host-shop_csrf cookie echoed in X-CSRF-Token; same-origin only; JSON; Cache-Control: no-store. Writes are ACTION-STYLE POSTs (there is no PATCH/PUT/DELETE on these routes): the body carries `action` plus the fields, and any key outside the allowlist is a 400 unknown_field:<name>.

post.description: Save (create or replace — a whole-row upsert, omitted optionals become null) the shopper's business identity: {action: "save", legal_name, ...}. The first save moves business_verification from unverified to self_declared. Same session + CSRF belt as POST /api/shop/addresses: cookie __Host-shop_session, and on POST the __Host-shop_csrf cookie echoed in X-CSRF-Token; same-origin only; JSON; Cache-Control: no-store. Writes are ACTION-STYLE POSTs (there is no PATCH/PUT/DELETE on these routes): the body carries `action` plus the fields, and any key outside the allowlist is a 400 unknown_field:<name>. contact_phone is E.164-normalised with country when a country is given.

address_id.description: One of the shopper's own address ids.

400.description: legal_name_required, invalid_business (hostile text, non-ISO country, non-http(s) website, bad phone), invalid_address, unknown_field:<name>, invalid_action.

403.description: cross_origin_rejected (not same-origin), CSRF token missing / mismatched / bound to a different session — or, on a write, business_customers_disabled when the store has allow_business_customers = 0 (403, not 400: the action is forbidden store-wide, not malformed — the checkout returns the same code as a 400 because there it is one more field validation).

429.description: Too many profile updates (60 per 5 minutes per IP) — or, on POST /api/shop/tax-ids add, too many tax ID checks (10 per hour per customer).

503.description: unavailable — this store is still finishing the upgrade that adds customer profiles (migration 0177); or store_not_provisioned.

get.description: The current cart: the signed-in shopper's (__Host-shop_session) or the guest cart the __Host-shop_cart token resolves to on this store. Reading never creates a cart. Prices are live; lines whose product is no longer sellable come back with available:false and are excluded from subtotal.

200.description: The cart. id is null and items empty when none exists yet.

post.description: Add a product to the cart, creating the cart if needed — a guest's first add mints the __Host-shop_cart cookie. Adding a product already in the cart sums quantities (capped at 999). Signed-in requests must echo __Host-shop_csrf in X-CSRF-Token. Rate limited per IP; sustained abuse returns 429.

200.description: The updated cart. A new guest cart also sets the __Host-shop_cart cookie.

400.description: invalid_product_id / invalid_quantity — non-integer, zero, negative or absurd values.

403.description: CSRF_INVALID — signed-in write without a valid X-CSRF-Token.

404.description: product_not_found — missing, archived, hidden, other-store, off-currency (a product listed in a currency other than the cart's) and absurdly-priced products are indistinguishable.

post.description: The form-encoded face of POST /api/shop/cart, posted by the product page's add-to-cart / buy-it-now form. Dispatches to the same add handler (same-origin, rate limit, CSRF, quantity and merge rules are identical), then answers by Accept: a browser (text/html) gets 303 to /checkout when checkout=1, else to /cart, with the guest cart cookie on the redirect; any other Accept gets POST /api/shop/cart's JSON verbatim. A sold-out product (stock 0, not flagged for oversell) is refused here with 409 out_of_stock — the JSON cart API still accepts such lines and checkout refuses them — and a browser is sent back to /products/{slug} on any failure.

checkout.description: Present (from the buy-it-now submit button) to be sent to /checkout instead of /cart on success.

csrf.description: The __Host-shop_csrf synchronizer, required for a signed-in shopper — the product page embeds it as a hidden field.

checkout.description: Present (from the buy-it-now submit button) to be sent to /checkout instead of /cart on success.

csrf.description: The __Host-shop_csrf synchronizer, required for a signed-in shopper — the product page embeds it as a hidden field.

200.description: Non-HTML clients: the updated cart, exactly as POST /api/shop/cart returns it.

303.description: Accept: text/html — Location is /checkout (checkout=1) or /cart on success. On failure, Location is /products/{slug} when the product resolves (active, visible, this store), else /cart (unknown, hidden or archived product). Set-Cookie carries a new guest cart token.

403.description: CSRF_INVALID — signed-in submit without the csrf field; cross_origin_rejected.

409.description: out_of_stock — stock is 0 and the product is not flagged for oversell.

post.description: Remember a coupon code on the cart once the evaluator accepts it (a code that is only waiting on a delivery country is accepted as pending). At most 3 codes per cart. Same gates as every cart write: same-origin, per-IP limiter, and signed-in requests must echo __Host-shop_csrf in X-CSRF-Token. Not a PAT surface — operators dry-run codes with POST /api/v1/discounts/validate.

400.description: invalid_code (malformed), cart_empty, too_many_codes, or code_rejected — `reason` says why in the shopper's words.

403.description: CSRF_INVALID.

503.description: store_not_provisioned, or discounts_unavailable while the store finishes its upgrade.

delete.description: Forget a code on the cart. Never a 404 — removing a code that is not there is a no-op that still returns the cart. Same gates as POST.

403.description: CSRF_INVALID.

patch.description: Set a cart line's quantity. The line must belong to the cart this request's own credentials resolve to — anyone else's line id returns the same 404 as a nonexistent one. Signed-in requests must echo __Host-shop_csrf in X-CSRF-Token.

403.description: CSRF_INVALID.

404.description: item_not_found — no such line in YOUR cart.

delete.description: Remove a cart line. Same ownership rule as PATCH. Signed-in requests must echo __Host-shop_csrf in X-CSRF-Token.

403.description: CSRF_INVALID.

404.description: item_not_found — no such line in YOUR cart.

post.description: Turn the current cart into an order. Guest checkout (__Host-shop_cart token) requires email and optionally name in the body and must be same-origin; the order's customer_id is null. Signed-in checkout (__Host-shop_session) must echo __Host-shop_csrf in X-CSRF-Token; contact fields come from the account, and the body may carry only payment_method_id, shipping_address, shipping_method_id and save_address (a bodyless POST is accepted). Line items snapshot name and the live price at checkout; totals are computed server-side in integer minor units — a client-supplied amount, price or currency is rejected by name, never used. Payment (slice 3b): while the store has NO enabled method backed by an implemented provider, checkout works exactly as before and records no payment; once it has at least one, a valid payment_method_id (an id from GET /api/shop/payment-methods) is REQUIRED, and the order gets a 'pending' payment row snapshotting the method's provider and name, with amount/currency taken from the order's own server-computed TOTAL (tax included) and currency. Choosing a method the offer excludes — a provider registered but not yet implemented (hyp), or a gateway provider with no credentials stored for the store's current gateway mode — is refused with 400 payment_method_unavailable before anything is written; the offer and this gate share one rule, so an id that is not offered cannot be accepted by posting it directly. For a gateway-backed method (payplus) the order and its pending payment row are created exactly the same way; the STOREFRONT checkout page then creates the provider payment session server-side and 302s the shopper to the provider-hosted payment page — this API response itself carries no payment link, and the payment is recorded only after server-side verification (gateway callback, or the shopper's return page re-triggering the same verification). The cart is consumed atomically (a guest's __Host-shop_cart cookie is cleared). Order status starts as pending_payment. Rate limited per IP. Tax (slice 5a): when the store has tax_enabled, the order is taxed with the store's current tax_rate and tax_inclusive and SNAPSHOTS both onto itself — tax_amount, tax_rate_bp (basis points, integer) and tax_inclusive are what it charged and the terms it charged under, never recomputed from settings afterwards. Prices that EXCLUDE tax add it on top (total = subtotal + tax_amount); prices that INCLUDE it keep total = subtotal and report the tax extracted out of it. With tax off the three are 0 and total = subtotal. Shipping (slice 5b-a): when the store has shipping_enabled, the body MUST carry shipping_address (see above), the store's flat rate is charged and the order SNAPSHOTS it — shipping_amount, shipping_label ('Shipping') and the six shipping_* address fields — so a later rate change, or a customer editing their address, cannot rewrite this receipt. total then includes the delivery charge, and the payment row books that same total. Tax and shipping share ONE base and ONE rounding: with the store's tax_shipping on, tax is computed over subtotal + shipping_amount, never over the two separately. With shipping off no address is collected or stored, shipping_amount is 0, shipping_label is null and total is exactly what it was before this release. Shipping zones and methods (slice 5b-b): when the store has one or more shipping ZONES configured, the flat rate no longer applies. The submitted shipping_address is matched to a zone server-side (country, then region; most specific wins), and the body must carry a shipping_method_id belonging to THAT zone — omitting it is 400 shipping_method_required, and an id that is unknown, disabled, another store's, or from a different zone is 400 invalid_shipping_method. Nothing is written on either refusal. The amount and the label come off the chosen method row (its free_over threshold, compared against the goods subtotal, can make it 0 — a labelled free delivery, not an absent one), never off the request, and the order additionally snapshots shipping_method_id for operator reporting; shipping_label stays what every surface renders, so deleting a method later cannot rewrite an old receipt. When zones exist and NONE matches the address — or the matching zone has no enabled method — the store does not deliver there and checkout is 400 no_delivery_coverage; it does NOT quietly fall back to the flat rate. With ZERO zones configured, behaviour is exactly slice 5b-a's: the store's flat rate, labelled 'Shipping', with shipping_method_id null. Address book (slice 5b-c): save_address, when exactly boolean true, saves shipping_address to the signed-in customer's address book (a new row, and their default if it is their first) AFTER the order succeeds — a refused or failed checkout saves nothing, however it was set. Ignored entirely for a guest checkout (no customer_id to save under) and for any other value (a truthy string is not accepted — the field must be the JSON boolean). The save is best-effort: a failure (including the address table being briefly absent during a platform upgrade) is logged and never fails the order. Tax engine T1 (spec 1.22.0): the order is priced by the store's tax RULES (store_tax_jurisdictions × store_tax_classes → rates, most specific jurisdiction for the taxable address) per line, half-up in integer minor units, the charged delivery split across the order's rate groups in proportion to their goods; with no rule for the address the store's tax_no_rule_fallback decides — flat (today's rate) or none (no tax; tax_breakdown.treatment not_registered). A tax-inclusive store prices under tax_inclusive_mode (fixed_gross: the listed price is what the shopper pays, the destination rate is extracted; fixed_net: the net at the home rate is fixed and destination tax goes on top — the difference lands in tax_adjustment). A store on the taxjar provider has standard orders priced by TaxJar; any provider failure is priced locally and recorded as tax_provider local_fallback. Each item carries its tax_amount / tax_rate_bp / tax_class_slug and the order its tax_breakdown / tax_provider / tax_adjustment; on a tenant mid-upgrade (columns absent) the order is priced flat and those keys echo the row defaults.

email.description: Required for guest checkout; ignored when signed in.

payment_method_id.description: Id of an enabled method from GET /api/shop/payment-methods. Required once the store has at least one enabled method with an implemented provider; omit while it has none.

shipping_address.description: The delivery address. REQUIRED when the store has shipping_enabled = 1 (guest and signed-in alike), and IGNORED — never rejected — when it has shipping off, so a stale client cannot break checkout. line1, city, postcode and country are required within it; line2 and region are optional. Any field failing the gate — control bytes, angle brackets, a non-string, over 200 characters, or a country that is not exactly two ASCII letters — is a single 400 invalid_shipping_address, and nothing is written. The address is SNAPSHOTTED onto the order (shipping_line1 … shipping_country); it is not a saved customer address. The delivery AMOUNT is never taken from this body — it is resolved server-side from the store's shipping settings, like the tax rate and the line prices.

region.description: State/province. Optional — many countries have none.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, case-insensitive on input and stored upper case. Exactly two ASCII letters — 'Israel' is a 400.

name.description: Recipient name (customer profile C1). Snapshotted as shipping_name (falls back to the order name).

phone.description: E.164-normalised with the address country; snapshotted as shipping_phone.

region_code.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code. Must be one of the country's subdivisions when the country has a list, and REQUIRED for US, CA, AU, BR, IN, MX (400 invalid_shipping_address / invalid_billing_address otherwise) — though a `region` text naming the subdivision ("TX", "Texas", "US-TX", any case) stands in for a missing code. Snapshotted as shipping_region_code / billing_region_code and used as the tax jurisdiction.

shipping_method_id.description: Id of a shipping method from the zone the shipping_address matches. REQUIRED once the store has at least one zone configured (400 shipping_method_required without it); omit while it has none, where the store-level flat rate applies instead. The zone is RE-DERIVED server-side from the submitted shipping_address before this id is honoured, so a method belonging to any other zone is refused (400 invalid_shipping_method) however its id was obtained — the rendered chooser is an offer, this is the gate. The PRICE is never taken from this body: it is read from the method row, with the method's own free_over threshold applied against the goods subtotal, and snapshotted onto the order as shipping_amount with the method's name as shipping_label.

save_address.description: Signed-in checkout only — ignored for a guest (no account to save to). When exactly `true`, shipping_address is saved to the customer's address book AFTER the order succeeds; any other value, or a checkout that fails, refuses coverage or is refused validation, saves nothing. The save is best-effort and never fails the order, even if it throws.

billing_address.description: Optional separate billing address; the same shape and gate as shipping_address (400 invalid_billing_address). Decides the tax jurisdiction when the store's tax_address_basis is billing.

region.description: State/province. Optional — many countries have none.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, case-insensitive on input and stored upper case. Exactly two ASCII letters — 'Israel' is a 400.

name.description: Recipient name (customer profile C1). Snapshotted as shipping_name (falls back to the order name).

phone.description: E.164-normalised with the address country; snapshotted as shipping_phone.

region_code.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code. Must be one of the country's subdivisions when the country has a list, and REQUIRED for US, CA, AU, BR, IN, MX (400 invalid_shipping_address / invalid_billing_address otherwise) — though a `region` text naming the subdivision ("TX", "Texas", "US-TX", any case) stands in for a missing code. Snapshotted as shipping_region_code / billing_region_code and used as the tax jurisdiction.

customer_type.description: Customer profile C1. Default individual. Anything else is 400 invalid_customer_type; business when the store has allow_business_customers = 0 is 400 business_customers_disabled. Snapshotted onto the order.

company.description: The buyer's company. Required (400 company_required) when customer_type is business and the store has require_company_for_business = 1.

phone.description: Guest arm; a member's phone comes from the account unless supplied. Required (400 phone_required) when the store has require_phone_at_checkout = 1.

tax_id.description: An inline tax ID, verified during checkout with the store's tax_id_verification (guests: in memory only, no row is created; members: alongside their saved IDs). A format failure is 400 invalid_tax_id with the type's label in reason; a provider outage does NOT block checkout — the order proceeds with standard treatment and the snapshot records status unavailable. Mutually exclusive with tax_id_id.

tax_id_id.description: Member arm: the id of one of the member's saved tax IDs (GET /api/shop/tax-ids). Another customer's or an unknown id is 400 invalid_tax_id. A saved ID still unverified / unavailable and older than 10 minutes is re-checked once, and the verdict persisted.

200.description: The order as placed: id, status pending_payment, currency, subtotal/total in minor units, the tax snapshot (tax_amount, tax_rate_bp, tax_inclusive), the shipping snapshot (shipping_amount, shipping_label and the six shipping_* address fields) and line items with snapshotted name, unit_price and line_total. total includes BOTH shipping and tax, so deriving tax as total - subtotal is wrong on a shipped order — read the fields. When a payment method was chosen, `payment` carries the method's display name and instructions for the confirmation page; it is absent when the store has no methods.

subtotal.description: The UNDISCOUNTED goods, in minor units.

discount_total.description: Discounts v1: goods discount + waived shipping, in minor units. 0 when nothing applied. Tax is computed on the discounted goods; a method's free_over is judged against the discounted goods too.

discounts.description: Discounts v1: what applied, snapshotted onto the order — [] when nothing did. A free-shipping entry has shipping: true and amount = the waived delivery price. A code the cart accepted that is refused only for the resolved country is dropped silently (it was shown as pending); one refused only because a usage cap was hit since is 409 discount_unavailable. shipping: true entries may carry amount 0 when the delivery was already free; the shipping line shows the price struck with the remainder.

total.description: Integer minor units, and what the payment row books: subtotal − discount_total + shipping_amount + tax_amount when tax_inclusive is 0, subtotal − discount_total + shipping_amount when it is 1. shipping_amount stays the chosen method's price even when a free-shipping discount waived it — the waiver is inside discount_total.

tax_amount.description: Tax charged, in minor units. 0 when the store has tax off.

tax_rate_bp.description: The rate this order was taxed at, in basis points (17.5% is 1750).

tax_inclusive.description: 1 when the listed prices already contained the tax (total = subtotal); 0 when it was added on top.

shipping_amount.description: Delivery charged on this order, in minor units, and included in total. 0 when the store has shipping off.

shipping_label.description: What the delivery line was called ('Shipping'); null when nothing was charged for delivery. This, not the amount, is the display gate — a free-shipping store has a label and a 0 amount.

shipping_country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, upper case. The address snapshot, all null when the store has shipping off.

discount.description: Discounts v1: this line's share of the goods discount (largest-remainder allocation), in minor units; 0 when none. line_total − discount is what the shopper paid for the line.

tax_amount.description: Tax engine T1 (migration 0211): this line's goods tax, minor units (the delivery's tax is not on any line). 0 when the columns are absent.

tax_rate_bp.description: The rate this line was taxed at, basis points (migration 0212); 0 under a zero-tax treatment.

tax_class_slug.description: The EFFECTIVE tax class (migration 0213): a class the jurisdiction has no rate for falls to 'standard' and says so. null when the columns are absent.

customer_type.description: Snapshotted at checkout (customer profile C1, migration 0193); individual on orders placed before it.

tax_treatment.description: What the tax engine decided (migration 0194). reverse_charge needs a business customer with a valid eu_vat ID in a different EU country than the store's origin_country; exempt is C2; not_taxable when the store has tax off. Never rewritten by later profile edits.

tax_jurisdiction.description: JSON {basis, country, region_code, id} — which address decided the taxable jurisdiction (migration 0195).

id.description: Tax engine T1: the store_tax_jurisdictions row that decided the rate, null on the flat fallback, under a zero-tax treatment, and on orders placed before migration 0204.

tax_id_snapshot.description: JSON {type, country, value, status} of the tax ID the treatment used — or the ID supplied even when treatment stayed standard (migration 0196). The FULL value: the receipt that used it must show it. null when none was given.

shipping_name.description: The address's recipient name, else the order name (migration 0187).

tax_breakdown.description: Tax engine T1 (migration 0215): the breakdown snapshot as written — {basis, country, region_code, jurisdiction_id, provider, mode: exclusive|fixed_gross|fixed_net, home_rate_bp, treatment, groups: [{class, rate_bp, goods, goods_tax, shipping, shipping_tax, shipping_taxed}], adjustment}. `treatment` is the engine's own word and is the only place `not_registered` (a `none` fallback with no rule for the address) appears — the tax_treatment column then reads not_taxable. TaxJar orders also carry `jurisdictions` (the provider's raw jurisdiction block). null on tenants that predate the column.

tax_provider.description: Who priced the order (migration 0216): the local engine, TaxJar, or the local engine standing in after a TaxJar failure (one audit_log row tax.provider.fallback). 'local' when the column is absent.

tax_adjustment.description: Migration 0217, signed minor units: what the shopper paid for the goods and delivery below (+) or above (−) the listed prices — fixed_net pricing, or a zero-tax treatment on a tax-inclusive store. total = subtotal − discount_total − tax_adjustment + shipping_amount + (exclusive ? tax_amount : 0). 0 when the column is absent.

payment.description: Present only when a payment method was chosen.

400.description: cart_empty (no cart, or nothing in it), invalid_email / invalid_name (guest fields), an unknown field — client-supplied totals are rejected — or a payment refusal: payment_method_required (the store has an enabled, implemented method but none was chosen), invalid_payment_method (unknown, disabled or another store's id), payment_method_unavailable (the method's provider — hyp — is registered but not yet implemented; nothing is written). Or a shipping refusal: invalid_shipping_address (see shipping_address), shipping_method_required (the store has zones but no method was chosen), invalid_shipping_method (unknown, disabled, another store's, or a method from a zone this address does not match), no_delivery_coverage (zones are configured and none serves this address, or the matching zone has no enabled method — the store does not deliver there). Nothing is written on any of them. Customer profile C1 adds: invalid_customer_type, business_customers_disabled (customer_type business while the store has allow_business_customers = 0 — 400 here, unlike the shopper profile endpoints' 403, because it is one more checkout validation), company_required, invalid_company (hostile text in company), phone_required, invalid_phone (a phone that cannot be normalised — a member re-posting the account's stored phone verbatim is always accepted), invalid_tax_id (format failure, or tax_id_id not this member's; reason names the type's label), invalid_billing_address.

403.description: CSRF_INVALID (signed-in, bad or missing X-CSRF-Token) or cross_origin_rejected (guest POST from another origin).

409.description: cart_unavailable_items — the cart holds a line whose product is archived, hidden, off-currency or over the price ceiling; product_ids names them. Remove those lines and retry. Or cart_insufficient_stock — a line asks for more units than the product has in stock; product_ids names the short lines (products with stock null are untracked and never refused). Reduce those quantities (or remove the lines) and retry. When a concurrent order took the last units mid-checkout the same code is returned with raced: true — there product_ids lists every line of the cart (the aborted transaction cannot say which line tripped), nothing was charged and the cart is intact. Or discount_unavailable (discounts v1) — a code the cart had accepted hit its total_limit or per_customer_limit since (another shopper redeemed the last use, or this email already used it); `code` names it and `reason` is the shopper-facing sentence. Nothing stays written (an order that had already committed in the narrowest race is undone, stock returned): remove the code (DELETE /api/shop/cart/discount/{code}) and retry.

413.description: body_too_large — the declared Content-Length exceeds the 16KB shop-API body cap.

503.description: store_not_provisioned — the tenant's store row does not exist yet.

get.description: The caller's own current consent decision, resolved from the `__Host-shop_consent` cookie. No cookie, no record, or the store not yet migrated all answer `{ ok:true, consent:null }`. A read NEVER mints a subject: no Set-Cookie is issued here. Returns the latest record only (the earlier rows are the controller's proof, not this response), and never the `subject_key`.

decision.description: The decision, as a FLAT map of key to boolean and nothing else. A key is either a tracker category (`strictly_necessary`, `analytics`, `marketing`) or one inventory entry's id (`__Host-shop_session`, `google_analytics`, ...); a per-entry key always wins over its category, because the remedy the EU rule pack names for a persistent login cookie is a per-cookie “remember me (uses cookies)” checkbox. Values MUST be booleans: a richer value such as `{granted:true}` would deny under an opt-in regime and allow under an opt-out one, the same stored decision meaning opposite things in two jurisdictions, so anything that is not a boolean — null included — is a 400 and is never coerced. An unknown key is a 400. `false` is how a refusal is recorded; null is never stored.

mode.description: The consent regime in force when the decision was recorded.

ui_version.description: Which banner text was shown — consent is to what was said. Server-set; never accepted from the caller.

expires_at.description: created_at + the validity period the rule pack states for this shopper. Null when no authority in scope states one — null means NO expiry was recorded, not a default.

withdrawn_at.description: Set only on a withdrawal row.

post.description:
Record a consent decision, or withdraw one. Unauthenticated by design — a first-time visitor answering the banner has no session, so no CSRF synchronizer can exist yet; same-origin is their guard, and once a shopper session IS present the X-CSRF-Token synchronizer is required like every other shopper write. Guards, in order: same-origin, 30 posts per IP per 5 minutes (SHOP_CONSENT_IP_LIMIT, the shared 100/min stacks), the field allowlist, CSRF when a session exists, then the store and the resolved policy.

The row written to `privacy_consent_records` proves a decision and identifies nobody: no IP address, no user agent, no e-mail. The subject is `subject_key`, a SHA-256 of the consent cookie's id salted with the store's own `consent_salt` — minted once, persisted, never rotated — so the same cookie id can never mean the same subject on two stores. The policy's own columns (mode, rule version, jurisdiction ids, confidence, validity) are picked by name; the resolved rule map itself is never stored.

WITHDRAWAL IS A NEW ROW. `{ withdraw:true }` inserts a second record with `withdrawn_at` set and every key the previous record carried turned to `false`; it never updates or deletes the earlier decision, which must stay readable to demonstrate the consent that was given. A body carrying both `decision` and `withdraw` is a 400.

Sets `__Host-shop_consent` (Path=/, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax), minting a 256-bit id on the first decision and keeping an existing well-formed one so a withdrawal lands on the same subject. Max-Age is the policy's validity period, and is omitted entirely (a session cookie) when no authority in scope states one.

An unknown key is a 400. `false` is how a refusal is recorded; null is never stored.

429.description: Rate limited (SHOP_CONSENT_IP_LIMIT, 30 per 5 minutes per IP).

503.description: store_not_provisioned | consent_unavailable (the ledger tables or the salt column have not reached this tenant yet — an unsalted pseudonym is not a row worth writing).

post.description: Redeem the cancel token from the deletion_requested mail (account integrity A1, D6). No session or CSRF. Clears `deletion_requested_at` and audits customer.deletion.cancelled. Signing in also cancels a pending deletion (POST /api/shop/login answers `deletion_cancelled: true`). The storefront page /account/delete/cancel/<token> shows a confirmation button on GET and posts here.

Ask for the account to be deleted (account integrity A1, D2/D6). Requires the shopper session, CSRF and `current_password` (the re-auth limiter). Refused with 409 open_orders while an order is pending_payment / paid / processing or a refund is pending. On success `deletion_requested_at` is stamped, every session destroyed and a `deletion_requested` mail with a single-use cancel link (/account/delete/cancel/<token>, 14 days) sent; the platform purges the account 14 days later unless cancelled by the link or by signing in. Audited as customer.deletion.requested.

post.description: Redeem the confirmation token mailed to the NEW address (account integrity A1, D4). No session or CSRF — the token is the secret. The row's pending_email must still match the token and the address must still be free and not held for another customer's live revert; then every session is destroyed, `email` becomes the new address (verified), and the revert link is extended to 14 days from now. Requires the shopper session, CSRF and `current_password` (per-customer limiters: 5 wrong attempts per 15 minutes, then 429; and 5 requests per hour once re-authenticated — a 409 counts — then 429). Sets `pending_email` and mails two single-use links: `email_change_confirm` to the NEW address (/account/email/confirm/<token>, 24 h) and `email_change_notice` to the OLD address (/account/email/revert/<token>, 14 days — the takeover defence: it restores the old address, ends every session and locks email changes for 24 h). Refused with 423 email_change_locked (body `until`: unix) for 24 h after a revert AND while a confirmed change's revert link is still live (one change per 14-day revert window — a second request would replace the owner's link). Audited as customer.email.change_requested with the new address masked.

Also clears a pending deletion request (and its cancel token). post.description: A storefront visitor submits a 'form' block (store-forms-p2). Unauthenticated — the largest public write in the store product. Guards, in order: same-origin, 5 posts per IP per hour (SHOP_FORM_IP_LIMIT), a honeypot field `website_url` that must stay empty (a filled one answers 200 with the same shape as success and stores nothing — checked BEFORE the block lookup, so a bot gets no signal from a 404 on a block id it invented), optional Cloudflare Turnstile verification (only when the store's `form_turnstile` setting AND the platform's TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY/TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY bindings are both present — a missing platform binding degrades to off rather than taking the form offline; a token that's missing, invalid, or unverifiable answers 400 `turnstile_failed`), the shopper session's CSRF synchronizer when signed in (X-CSRF-Token header or `csrf` field — a guest needs none), then block resolution. `block_id` must resolve to a block that is active, published, `block_type='form'`, and a member of the set of blocks the storefront page named by `page` actually renders (accounts for template inheritance via `parent_template_id`). `page` is the path the form lives on, e.g. `/pages/contact`; when omitted the request URL is used, which is only a page for the in-process dispatch from `/pages/:slug` — a direct call without `page` therefore 404s. Naming the page grants nothing a `POST /pages/:slug` did not already: the check binds the block to a live, published custom page that renders it, never to the page a human was looking at — any mismatch (unknown, foreign, unpublished, inactive, or on a different page) answers a flat 404 with no distinguishing detail. Field values are validated against the block's own field definitions (`utils/form-schema.js` validateSubmission); an unknown posted key is never read, let alone stored. `ip_hash` is `sha256(ip + TOKEN_SECRET)`, never the raw address. Always answers JSON — the page route (`pages/[slug].js`) turns `ok:true` into a 303 redirect to `?sent=<blockId>` and any other status into a same-page re-render with the typed values and, for a 429, CSRF-expired 403, or Turnstile-failed 400, a form-level message.

csrf.description: Required only when the POST carries a signed-in shopper session cookie.

additionalProperties.description: One entry per field key the form block defines (e.g. name, email, message).

page.description: Storefront path of the page the form block renders on (e.g. `/pages/contact`). Required for a direct call; the in-process dispatch from `/pages/:slug` supplies it from the request URL. Only the pathname is read.

cf-turnstile-response.description: Cloudflare Turnstile widget token, only required when the store has Turnstile enabled and the platform binding is present.

200.description: Stored (or the honeypot was tripped — indistinguishable from a real success).

400.description: invalid_body | turnstile_failed: { ok:false, error:'turnstile_failed' } (Turnstile on, token missing/invalid/unverifiable — fails closed, including an unreachable siteverify) | per-field validation errors: { ok:false, errors: { <fieldKey>: 'required' | 'invalid' } }

404.description: not_found — unknown, inactive, unpublished, wrong block_type, not rendered on the page `page` names, or `page` missing/unresolvable. No further detail, by design.

post.description: Shopper sign-in. Sets the __Host-shop_session (HttpOnly) and __Host-shop_csrf cookies. If a __Host-shop_cart guest-cart token rides along, that guest cart merges into the customer's cart on this store (same product sums quantities, capped at 999; products in only one cart carry over) and the __Host-shop_cart cookie is expired — the guest token is invalidated. Cross-site POSTs (mismatched Origin header) are rejected with 403 before anything else. Every credential failure mode — unknown email, wrong password, disabled account — returns one identical 401. Rate limited per IP and per (email, IP); sustained failure returns 429 before credentials are checked.

200.description: Signed in; __Host-shop_session + __Host-shop_csrf cookies set. Any guest cart was merged and its __Host-shop_cart cookie expired.

deletion_cancelled.description: Present (true) when this sign-in cancelled a pending deletion request (account integrity A1, D6).

401.description: invalid_credentials — one response for every failure mode.

403.description: cross_origin_rejected — the Origin header names another site (login CSRF protection).

parameters.name: X-CSRF-Token
parameters.description: The __Host-shop_csrf cookie value (HMAC-bound to this session).

403.description: CSRF token missing, mismatched, or bound to a different session.

Empty string clears the phone. Requires the session cookie and the X-CSRF-Token synchronizer.

On success every session is destroyed and the caller's is re-minted — the response carries fresh __Host-shop_session / __Host-shop_csrf cookies — and a `password_changed` mail with a single-use "secure my account" link (/account/secure/<token>, 14 days) goes to the account address. 403.description: reauth_failed — wrong current password; or CSRF_INVALID / cross_origin_rejected.

429.description: Five wrong current passwords in 15 minutes.

post.description: Redeem a password-reset token and set a new password. The token is single-use; unknown, expired and already-used tokens return one identical 400. On success every existing shopper session for that customer is revoked and no new session is started — sign in at /api/shop/login with the new password. Rate limited per IP.

token.description: 64-char lowercase hex token from the reset link.

password.description: Min 8 chars with upper, lower and digit.

400.description: Invalid, expired or already-used token, or weak password.

Always returns the same generic success whether or not the email belongs to a customer, so it cannot enumerate customer emails. Mints a single-use reset token valid for 1 hour, stored only as a SHA-256 hash; the link is mailed to the account address as /account/reset/<token> (nothing is sent for an unknown address, and the response does not say which). Rate limited per IP and per (email, IP).

200.description: Generic success — identical for known and unknown emails.

get.description: The checkout OFFER: the payment methods a shopper may actually pay with — only rows that are enabled by the operator, backed by an implemented provider, and (for a gateway provider) backed by credentials actually stored for the store's CURRENT gateway mode. A configured hyp method is deliberately NOT offered (registered but not yet implemented; nothing can take money through it until a later release). A payplus method is offered only once its credentials for the store's current mode are saved — payplus is implemented via the redirect flow, but offering it unconfigured would place an order and hold stock for a payment that can never start. Offline methods (bank_transfer, cash_on_delivery) need no credentials and are never gated on one. No authentication; per-IP rate limited.

200.description: The offered methods, sort_order then name. Only shopper-facing fields — never enabled, sort_order or timestamps.

post.description: The payment gateway's server-to-server notification (IPN) for a redirect payment — called by the provider, not by browsers, PATs or agents. Only payplus is implemented in this release: hyp (registered but not yet implemented) and any unknown provider are a 404. The callback body is treated as an untrusted hint: the tenant looks the claimed transaction up against the provider's own API (using the store's saved gateway credentials for its configured gateway_mode) and only a transaction that verifies as an approved charge, created for that exact order, for the order's exact total and currency, records the payment (the pending payment row goes received with the provider transaction id as reference) and moves the order pending_payment → paid through the standard order state machine. A verified charge for an order that has already settled (paid, shipped, refunded, cancelled) never moves the order; instead it is recorded as a reconcilable kind='orphan' payment row on the order — the double-charge evidence, visible in the order's payments list — which never counts toward refundable_amount. A well-formed callback is ALWAYS acknowledged with 200 whether or not it verified — the response reveals nothing about orders, credentials or verification — and a replayed callback for an already-recorded transaction reference is a 200 no-op. Only a malformed (non-JSON-object) body is a 400. Per-IP rate limited. The shopper's return to the storefront (/checkout/return, a page, not an API route) independently re-triggers the same server-side verification, so a lost callback does not lose the payment.

schema.description: The provider's IPN payload, passed through as-is. Only two fields are consulted, and both only as lookup keys: transaction_uid (the provider transaction to verify) and more_info (the order id the payment session was created for). Nothing in the body is ever trusted as the outcome.

200.description: Acknowledged. Returned for every well-formed callback — verified, unverified, unknown order, or replay — so the gateway stops retrying; whether anything was recorded is deliberately not disclosed.

post.description: Open a data-subject request — access, rectification, erasure, portability, restriction or objection (P8, design §3/§5). Same-origin required; CSRF required once a shopper session exists. IDENTITY: being signed in IS the verification (Art. 12(6) permits asking for more only where there are reasonable doubts), so a signed-in request opens as `open` with no second step, ever. A request without a session is answered with a one-time link (24 h) to the address ALREADY ON FILE and stays `verifying` until that link is followed; an address with no account produces no request and the SAME response, so this endpoint is not an account-enumeration oracle. No document upload, photo, date of birth or security question is ever requested, on any response. `erasure` requires `current_password` because it routes to the live POST /api/shop/deletion/request, which re-authenticates and refuses with 409 open_orders while an order is pending. The register stores NO request body, NO e-mail address and NO IP: the subject is a per-store salted hash, and the requester's own words travel to the operator by e-mail instead. The response deadline is computed at RECEIPT from the rule pack (strictest applicable wins) and `due_at` is null when no rule in force states one — never a substituted default. Following the link later does not move `received_at`. ROUTING: a verified `erasure` is handed to the live deletion flow and answers with its status and its session-clearing Set-Cookie headers (`status: routed`, `routed_to: deletion_request`; a 409 open_orders is recorded as `refused` with the reason, because a refusal is an answer and has its own deadline); `objection` is handed to POST /api/shop/consent's withdrawal, the same opt-out mechanism the footer link uses, and answers with its consent cookie (`routed_to: consent_withdrawal`); `rectification` names the existing account profile surfaces (`routed_to: account_profile`) and stays `open`; a SIGNED-IN `access` or `portability` request is routed to the export that already exists (`status: routed`, `routed_to: account_export`, `download_path: /account/export`) — GET /account/export is session-gated, rate-limited 3 per 24 h, `private, no-store` and streamed, so there is no stored file and no URL, and P9 points at it rather than building, mailing or minting a link to a second one. A requester who only redeemed the verification link has proved the ADDRESS and not the session, so nothing is routed and nothing is attached: the redemption page tells them to sign in and use Download your data, the row stays `open`, and the operator is notified. An unverified request routes nowhere at all. Routing is still not fulfilment: `answered` is never written here, no response, page or e-mail carries a link to the document or a filename, and the 3-per-24h export limit is untouched.

email.description: Only for a request with no session: the address to send the one-time link to. It must already be on file.

note.description: The requester's own message. Forwarded to the operator by e-mail and deliberately NOT stored in the register.

current_password.description: Required for `kind: erasure` — the re-auth the live deletion flow performs.

token.description: Redeem a one-time verification link instead of opening a request. The token is the secret, so no session and no CSRF are required; one use only, and `received_at` is not moved.

200.description: Opened (`status: open`, with `due_at` and `deadline_rule`), handed to an existing flow (`status: routed`, with `routed_to`, plus `download_path` for access/portability), accepted pending verification (`status: verifying`, deliberately carrying no deadline), or a redeemed link (`status: open` with `kind`, `received_at`, `due_at`, `deadline_rule`).

routed_to.description: `deletion_request`, `consent_withdrawal`, `account_profile` or `account_export` — the flow that already exists and now holds this request. Null for a request that has not been verified.

download_path.description: `/account/export`, present only on a signed-in `access` or `portability` request. A PATH, never a URL, and never a filename: the export is streamed from behind the requester's own session and no stored copy exists.

received_at.description: Unix seconds. The clock starts at receipt, never at verification.

due_at.description: Null when no rule in force for this requester states a response deadline. Null means UNKNOWN, not a default.

429.description: Too many requests, per IP or per subject address (keyed on the hash, never the address).

503.description: consent_unavailable or privacy_requests_unavailable — the upgrade window before the P7/P8 migrations land.

post.description: Redeem a verification token (account integrity A1, D1). No session or CSRF — the token is the secret. Consumes it (single use, 24 h) and stamps email_verified_at = COALESCE(email_verified_at, now). The storefront page /account/verify/<token> does the same on GET.

get.description: The store tenant’s public profile. Served by store tenants, not CMS tenants. No authentication.
