get.description: Export templates and pages as a single template-bundle JSON file. Portable between tenant sites: cross-entity references travel in a per-block `refs` list of RFC 6901 JSON Pointers carrying slugs, so the `config` object stays byte-exact and valid against the block's own schema. The parent chain of every selected template is included automatically and marked `included: "dependency"` - a template without its base layout renders with no header and no footer. `theme` is recorded for forward compatibility and is NOT applied on import; this product has no per-tenant theme. Requires the editor role: a bundle carries every selected design and, with `content=1`, every selected page's body including drafts. Read-only tokens may call this, as long as their user holds that role.

parameters.name: siteWide
parameters.description: 1 includes every base layout, i.e. header/footer/nav blocks. Default 0.

400.description: Nothing selected, an unknown slug, or a cap exceeded.

post.description: Decide everything a template-bundle import would do, and write nothing. The same decision engine backs apply (import is applied in a later endpoint): a slug collision with no entry in `onCollision` makes the plan `valid: false` rather than guessing - overwriting is destructive and suffixing leaves the old URL 404ing with no CMS redirect table to catch it. An unknown block type or a config that fails its own block-type schema also makes the plan invalid; every cross-entity reference this site cannot resolve, every media reference pointing at another site, and every field the importer rejected (unsafe customCss, form-control attributes stripped from imported HTML) is reported rather than silently applied or dropped. HTTP 200 with `valid: false` is correct - this is a report on a bundle, not an attempt to use it. Editor role or above required.

onCollision.description: Per-item collision decision, in TWO keyspaces: `templates` keyed by the template's `ref` (or its `slug`, checked second), `pages` keyed by the page's `slug`. A flat map is refused with a 400 naming both keyspaces - a template and a page may share a slug, and one shared key applied a page's 'overwrite' to the same-named template as well, deleting its zones and blocks. Overwrite is the only irreversible path here (the CMS keeps no template history), so an ambiguous key is never guessed.

templates.description: Keyed by the template's `ref`, or its `slug`.

onUnresolved.description: Accepted here too, so a preview shows what 'drop' would do to each block. 'fail' (default) rejects the whole import if any cross-entity reference cannot resolve on this site - a design that silently lost its category filter looks right and is wrong. 'drop' imports anyway and, per reference, either nulls the pointer (where that block's own schema permits null, reported as `action: "nulled"`) or skips the whole block (where it does not, reported as `action: "block_skipped"`). It never leaves the exporting site's id in place: that id resolves to an unrelated local row and the block renders against the wrong thing.

200.description: The full decision - see `valid` for whether it can be applied as-is.

400.description: Body is not valid JSON. Note that a bundle which is merely invalid (including an out-of-charset or over-long slug, or nesting past the depth cap) is a 200 with valid:false and the reasons in `errors`.

403.description: Editor role required.

413.description: Bundle exceeds the byte cap; the body names the cap.

post.description: Apply a template-bundle import. Runs the same decision engine as /api/templates/import/preview, then writes everything in ONE db.batch: nothing is written if any block fails its own schema, any reference is unresolved (unless onUnresolved:'drop'), or any collision has no entry in `onCollision`. A reserved slug is NOT one of those conditions - it is skipped (see TemplateImportPlan.templates[].action), so an unmodified export applies cleanly even though every export carries `default-base`. This route returns 400 exactly when the preview's `valid` is false and 200 otherwise: there is one decision engine and this route adds no verdict of its own. A CREATED template or page lands status='draft', is_default=0 and is therefore inert until published. An OVERWRITE replaces a live design or page body IMMEDIATELY and cannot be undone: it rewrites the target's zones and blocks and deliberately leaves status and is_default alone, so a published target stays published, carrying the imported content from the next request onward. Note that templates.status is NOT consulted by any renderer, so it cannot be relied on to keep an imported design offline. Imported HTML is sanitised on the way in and what was removed is reported in `rejected`. Requires admin, not merely editor: one call can overwrite many designs at once.

onCollision.description: Per-item collision decision, in TWO keyspaces: `templates` keyed by the template's `ref` (or its `slug`, checked second), `pages` keyed by the page's `slug`. A flat map is refused with a 400 naming both keyspaces - a template and a page may share a slug, and one shared key applied a page's 'overwrite' to the same-named template as well, deleting its zones and blocks. Overwrite is the only irreversible path here (the CMS keeps no template history), so an ambiguous key is never guessed.

templates.description: Keyed by the template's `ref`, or its `slug`.

onUnresolved.description: 'fail' (default) rejects the whole import if any cross-entity reference cannot resolve on this site - a design that silently lost its category filter looks right and is wrong. 'drop' imports anyway and, per reference, either nulls the pointer (where that block's own schema permits null, reported as `action: "nulled"`) or skips the whole block (where it does not, reported as `action: "block_skipped"`). It never leaves the exporting site's id in place: that id resolves to an unrelated local row and the block renders against the wrong thing.

400.description: Nothing was written: body is not valid JSON, the bundle is invalid, a slug contained a path separator or a dot-dot segment, contained a control character or exceeded 200 characters, a block config nested deeper than 64 levels, `onCollision` was sent as one flat map instead of {templates,pages}, a collision had no decision, or (with the default onUnresolved:'fail') a reference did not resolve on this site. Every reason is named in the body - never a bare status.

403.description: Admin role required.

413.description: Bundle exceeds the byte cap; the body names the cap.

get.description: The site's design tokens: tokens.json with the site palette (`theme_palette`) merged in — primary/accent ramps and `colors.site`. Identical to the base tokens for a site with no palette. Served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60`.

The caller's own user row (never includes credential columns), plus `readOnly` — true when authenticating with a read-only PAT — and `authMethod` (`pat` or `session`). Use it as the first call of a session to learn your role and whether the token may write. Both products serve this call under /api/v1 (GET /api/v1/users/me) and answer with `product`, so one request identifies any tenant; this bare /api path is CMS-only.

product.description: Which EdgePress product this tenant runs: "cms" (absent also means cms) or "store".

get.description: BOTH products serve this path. On CMS tenants it is the /api/v1 mirror of /api/api-tokens (documented there); on STORE tenants this /api/v1 path is the only one. Lists personal access tokens by masked `prefix` — the raw secret is never returned after creation. Non-admin callers see their own tokens; admins see every user's (each row then carries `user`). Works with a PAT, for audits.

post.description: BOTH products serve this path. On CMS tenants it is the /api/v1 mirror of /api/api-tokens (documented there); on STORE tenants this /api/v1 path is the only one. Mints a token. SESSION-ONLY: a request authenticated with a PAT is refused with 403 `session_required` (a leaked token must not mint more) — send the user to the admin UI at `/admin/settings/api-tokens`. The raw `token` is returned exactly once, in this response; only its SHA-256 is stored.

expiresInDays.description: Omit for a token that never expires.

readOnly.description: true → GET/HEAD only; any write is 403 read_only_token.

201.description: Created — the only time the raw token is visible

delete.description: BOTH products serve this path. On CMS tenants it is the /api/v1 mirror of /api/api-tokens (documented there); on STORE tenants this /api/v1 path is the only one. Soft-revokes a token (owner or admin): it is refused with 401 `invalid_token` from the next request on, and stays in the list as `revoked: true` for audit history. SESSION-ONLY: 403 `session_required` when called with a PAT. Idempotent — revoking an already-revoked token is another 204.

404.description: not_found — no such token, or not yours

post.description: Mint a 15-minute preview token for a pending storefront theme without saving it. `theme` is validated exactly like PATCH /api/v1/settings (rawCss sanitised, serialized size at most 4000 bytes). The returned `url` (`/?ep_theme_preview=<token>`) renders the storefront with that theme for anyone holding it — share-safe by design, bounded by the TTL. Write tokens only.

400.description: Invalid JSON, theme missing or not an object, rawCss rejected, or theme over 4000 bytes.

get.description: The store's audit log — who did what, when, from where — NEWEST FIRST, keyset-paged on `id`. Take `next_before` from one response and send it back as `?before=` for the next page; it is null on the last page. Filters AND together and match exactly (no substring). On CMS tenants this same path is the /api/v1 mirror of the CMS's /api/audit-log (offset-paged, `{entries, total, limit, offset}`, admin-only) — a different envelope; product-detect with GET /api/store first. On the store, authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may GET. The same rows back the admin UI at `/admin/settings/audit-log`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Non-numeric or 0 falls back to 50; values above 200 are capped, values below 1 raised to 1.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Return rows with id strictly below this — the previous page's `next_before`. Given but not a positive integer is a 400, refused rather than silently restarted from the top.

parameters.name: user_email
parameters.description: Exact match on the actor's email as recorded at the time.

next_before.description: Send as `?before=` for the next (older) page; null when this is the last page.

400.description: `before` given but not a positive integer.

get.description: List all available block types for the template editor. Results ordered by sort_order ASC, type_slug ASC. Cached for 300s per store; pass ?fresh=1 to bypass cache.

503.description: Schema not yet provisioned (pre-0108 tenant) or store not provisioned

get.description: Get the JSON Schema for a single block type by slug. The schema field is returned as a parsed object.

503.description: Schema not yet provisioned (pre-0108 tenant) or store not provisioned

get.description: List the store’s categories, ordered by sort_order then name. Products reference these ids via /api/v1/products. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET. Response envelope: { data, total, counts }. `total` is data.length for THIS response (page size after filters/limit), not a whole-store row count. `counts` is whole-store and filter-independent — it drives tab labels, not the current page. Every row carries product_count (direct members) and rules (null = manual).

total.description: Always equals data.length — the current page/result-set size, NOT a whole-store COUNT.

counts.description: Categories have no enabled/disabled or status concept, so this is just the whole-store row count.

post.description: Create a category. name is required; slug defaults to a slug derived from name. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

slug.description: Defaults to a slug derived from name. Must be unique across the store.

parent_id.description: Id of an existing category, or null for top level.

rules.description: Set to make the category automatic (membership is materialized immediately); null makes it manual again, keeping its current rows. 503 on a tenant still receiving the migration.

field_presets.description: Replace the category's detail fields; null clears them. Duplicate keys or a select without options are 400.

400.description: Missing name, or parent_id names no existing category

409.description: A category with this slug already exists

post.description: Applies one action (show/hide set is_visible=1/0; delete removes the row, detaching children) to many categories rows at once. Every id must belong to THIS store — if ANY id is missing or owned by another store, the WHOLE request is rejected with 400 cross_store_or_missing_ids:<ids> and NOTHING is applied (no partial application of a hostile or stale id list). Idempotent per id — applying the same action twice is a no-op. At most 500 ids per call. Served by STORE tenants only; read-only tokens may not POST.

ids.description: store_categories row ids owned by this store.

applied.description: Number of ids the action was applied to — equals ids.length on success (all-or-nothing).

400.description: body must be an object; unknown_action:<action>; ids_required; ids_must_be_positive_integers; too_many_ids (>500); cross_store_or_missing_ids:<ids>

post.description: Dry-run a smart-category rule set: the number of this store's products that match right now and the first 50 of them. Writes nothing — call it while composing rules, before saving them on a category. Served by STORE tenants only; read-only tokens may only GET.

put.description: Move and reorder categories in one write — what the admin's drag-and-drop tree editor sends on every drop. Body names only the nodes that changed; each gets its new parent_id (null = top level) and sort_order among its siblings. Every id must be one of this store's categories (404 otherwise), every parent_id a store category or null (400), and the RESULTING tree must be acyclic — checked over the current rows merged with the payload, so a cycle formed by two moved nodes is caught too (400 'the move would create a category cycle'). One batch: nothing applies unless everything does. Served by STORE tenants only; read-only tokens may only GET.

400.description: Malformed node, unknown parent, or the move would create a cycle

404.description: A node id is not a category of this store

get.description: Fetch one category. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

patch.description: Partial update; send only the fields to change. A category cannot be its own parent. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET. Changing `slug` records the previous one as rename history: the old URL then 301s to the new one, and any migration redirect that pointed at the old slug is repointed, so inbound links stay at one hop.

slug.description: Defaults to a slug derived from name. Must be unique across the store.

parent_id.description: Id of an existing category, or null for top level.

rules.description: Set to make the category automatic (membership is materialized immediately); null makes it manual again, keeping its current rows. 503 on a tenant still receiving the migration.

field_presets.description: Replace the category's detail fields; null clears them. Duplicate keys or a select without options are 400.

409.description: A category with this slug already exists

delete.description: Delete a category. Child categories are detached (parent_id set to null), not deleted; product–category links are removed. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

post.description: Upload the category's image (multipart/form-data, field `file`: JPEG/PNG/WebP/AVIF ≤25 MB). Runs through the same AVIF pipeline as product images; three variants land in the store's media bucket under categories/{id}/ and image_url is set to the large one (shown as the category-page banner and in the category-nav block's cards layout). Replaces a previous upload. Served by STORE tenants only; read-only tokens may not POST.

400.description: Not an accepted image, too large, or no file

502.description: The image could not be processed or saved — `error` is a plain sentence, `detail` the technical cause

503.description: Uploads not available on this store yet

delete.description: Clear image_url and remove the uploaded variants (a third-party URL is simply cleared).

get.description: The category's products in its own storefront order (position), each with is_primary and a thumbnail. Any status — this is the operator view. Served by STORE tenants only; read-only tokens may only GET.

put.description: REPLACE the category's membership and order in one batch: position in product_ids becomes each product's position; ids absent from the array leave the category; [] empties it. Every id must be a product of this store (400 otherwise). On a smart category the rules re-assert membership immediately afterwards, so the call is effectively a reorder. 503 on a tenant still receiving the per-category order migration. Served by STORE tenants only; read-only tokens may only GET.

200.description: OK — the category's products after the write

get.description: List the store's shopper accounts, newest first — active and disabled alike. Rows never include password_hash or the account's live phone number. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET. Response envelope: { data, total, counts }. `total` is data.length for THIS response (page size after filters/limit), not a whole-store row count. `counts` is whole-store and filter-independent — it drives tab labels, not the current page. Customer profile C1 (1.21.0): rows also carry phone, email_verified_at, customer_type, tax_status (best across the customer's tax IDs) and company (the business legal_name) — read through guarded joins, so on a tenant still finishing the 0177-0181 migrations the list answers with the defaults (individual / none / null) rather than failing. C2 (1.23.0): rows carry tags (names) and pending_exemptions (count); filter with ?tag=<slug> and ?pending_exemptions=1.

total.description: Always equals data.length — the current page/result-set size, NOT a whole-store COUNT.

counts.description: Whole-store aggregate — NOT a per-row filter flag on each customer.

parameters.name: after_id
parameters.description: Cursor: rows with id < after_id (pages are 100 rows, id DESC; has_more when data.length === 100).

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Only customers carrying this tag (slug or name; C2 1.23.0). An unknown tag — or a tenant without the tags table yet — gives an empty page.

parameters.name: pending_exemptions
parameters.description: Only customers with at least one tax exemption awaiting review (C2 1.23.0); empty page pre-0227.

post.description: Applies one action to many customers rows at once. Every id must belong to THIS store — if ANY id is missing or owned by another store, the WHOLE request is rejected with 400 cross_store_or_missing_ids:<ids> and NOTHING is applied (no partial application of a hostile or stale id list). Idempotent per id — applying the same action twice is a no-op. At most 500 ids per call. Served by STORE tenants only; read-only tokens may not POST.

ids.description: store_customers row ids owned by this store.

applied.description: Number of ids the action was applied to — equals ids.length on success (all-or-nothing).

400.description: body must be an object; unknown_action:<action>; ids_required; ids_must_be_positive_integers; too_many_ids (>500); cross_store_or_missing_ids:<ids>

501.description: action: 'export' is accepted but not implemented — no CSV export backend in v1

patch.description: Enable/disable a shopper and edit the operator-owned profile fields. Body is any of: status ('active' or 'disabled'), customer_type, business_verification (only manually_verified, or back to self_declared — the pipeline states are the pipeline's), operator_notes (≤ 4000 characters or null). Disabling destroys every live storefront session the shopper holds, immediately — and re-enabling does NOT revive them: the shopper must log in again. Idempotent: re-asserting the current status is a 200, not a 409. An unknown body field is a 400 unknown_field:<name>, never silently ignored. Another store's customer id, an unknown id or a malformed id is a plain 404. Every call writes an audit_log row (action customer.profile.update; details name the fields, operator_notes only as changed:true). Profile fields on a tenant that has not run 0177 are 503 customer_profiles_unavailable; status alone still works there. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET. C2 (1.23.0): `tags` replaces the operator-only tag set; the audit row lists the tag names.

status.description: The target status. Disabling kills all live sessions; re-enabling restores the ability to log in, never old sessions.

tags.description: REPLACE the customer's tags (C2 D7): names, deduped by slug, unknown names create store tags exactly as the product write does; null or [] clears. 503 customer_tags_unavailable pre-0230.

status.description: The status after the call (unchanged when the body did not carry one).

profile.description: The profile after the call; null on a pre-0177 tenant.

400.description: Validation failed — bad status value, invalid_customer_type, invalid_business_verification, an over-long operator_notes, unknown_field:<name>, an empty or non-object body. tags (C2): `tags must be an array of at most 30 names, or null`, `tags[i] must be a string`, `tags[i] must be 1-40 characters`, `tags[i] needs at least one letter or digit`.

503.description: customer_profiles_unavailable — this store is still finishing the upgrade that adds customer profiles (migrations 0177-0181); retry shortly; customer_tags_unavailable when the body carries tags on a tenant still finishing migration 0230 (no tag rows are written — profile fields already sent in the same request are saved).

get.description: One shopper in full (customer profile C1): identity, profile, business identity, MASKED tax IDs (the full value is on GET …/tax-ids/{tid}), the address book, and orders_count / total_spend (COUNT(*) and SUM(total) over the customer's orders whose status is not cancelled, refunded or pending_payment). Never 503s for the upgrade window: on a tenant that has not run 0177 profile is null and tax_ids is []. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET. C2 (1.23.0): the detail also carries tags and exemptions. A1 (1.24.0): pending_email, deletion_requested_at and gated; actions live at …/verify, …/resend-verification, …/cancel-deletion and …/export.

404.description: No such customer (or tax ID) — another store's id, an unknown id or a malformed id are all this same plain 404.

get.description: The shopper's address book, READ ONLY — the book is the shopper's to edit; the operator reads it to understand an order or a tax jurisdiction. Default shipping address first, then by id. [] when the tenant has no address book yet. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

404.description: No such customer (or tax ID) — another store's id, an unknown id or a malformed id are all this same plain 404.

post.description: Cancel the shopper's pending account-deletion request (account integrity A1, D12; spec 1.24.0): clears deletion_requested_at and kills the shopper's cancel-by-link token, so the 14-day purge no longer applies. The shopper's sessions were already destroyed when they requested deletion; they simply sign in again. No body. Audit: customer.deletion.cancel. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

404.description: No such customer — another store's id, an unknown id or a malformed id are all this same plain 404.

409.description: not_pending — no deletion request is pending for this customer.

get.description: List a customer's tax exemptions, newest first, with `effective_status` (an approved row past expires_at reads `expired` — status is stored, expiry is lazy) and the operator document URL. Envelope { data, total }; { data: [], total: 0 } on a tenant still finishing migration 0227. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

404.description: No such customer — another store's id, an unknown id or a malformed id are all this same plain 404 (error "Customer not found").

post.description: Create a tax exemption on behalf of a customer (submitted_by 'operator'). Discount fields. kind: percent (value = basis points, 1000 = 10%), fixed (value = integer minor units, allocated across eligible lines largest-remainder), free_shipping (value must be 0). code: 3-32 of A-Z 0-9 _ -, uppercased on save; omit or null for an AUTOMATIC discount that applies to every cart. scope defaults to {type: order}; every id/slug named must exist in this store (400 `scope ids not found`). conditions defaults to {}. usage_count is checkout's counter and is never writable (400 unknown_field:usage_count). kind bxgy (Buy X get Y): send `reward` — required for kind bxgy, refused (400) on any other kind; value is forced to 0 and scope to {type: order}, and reward.buy.scope / reward.get.scope are store-checked like scope. delivery discounts are percent/fixed rows with applies_to: shipping (503 discounts_unavailable while the store is finishing the upgrade that adds the column). conditions.shipping_methods ids must be this store's (400 `shipping method ids not found`). Changing kind away from bxgy drops the stored reward; changing kind TO bxgy needs a reward in the same PATCH unless one is stored; a bare `reward` re-validates against the stored kind.

code.description: Uppercased on save. null / omitted = automatic discount.

value.description: percent: basis points 1-10000; fixed: minor units ≥ 1; free_shipping / bxgy: 0 (forced).

applies_to.description: shipping: a percent/fixed discount taken off the charged delivery price (capped at it); refused on bxgy and free_shipping. Sent alone, the stored kind stands in; a kind change to bxgy/free_shipping resets it to goods

reward.description: Required for kind bxgy; refused otherwise. On PATCH, null is only accepted together with a non-bxgy kind.

combinable.description: Default true. A non-combinable discount that wins applies alone; codes it displaces are rejected with `Can't be combined with <title>`.

priority.description: Higher applies first (then larger standalone amount, then lower id). Default 0.

ends_at.description: Unix seconds; null = no end. Must be after starts_at.

400.description: Validation error, unknown_field:<name>, No updatable fields provided, or `scope ids not found`.

409.description: code_taken

503.description: discounts_unavailable — this store is still finishing the upgrade that adds discounts; retry shortly.

delete.description: Delete a discount that was never redeemed. 409 has_redemptions once any order used it — redemptions are order history; archive it instead (PATCH {status: archived} or POST /bulk archive).

409.description: has_redemptions

503.description: discounts_unavailable — this store is still finishing the upgrade that adds discounts; retry shortly.

get.description: Who used this discount: one row per order it was applied to, newest first. `total` is the full count; `data` is capped by ?limit= (default 50, max 500).

503.description: discounts_unavailable — this store is still finishing the upgrade that adds discounts; retry shortly.

get.description: Report whether this store has a connected Brevo account: configured, the visible from_address/from_name and both timestamps — never the API key. There is no read-back call for the key by design (write-only, the same rule gateway credentials follow): an owner who has lost it reconnects it from Brevo's own dashboard, through PUT. No master-key gate here — a missing platform encryption binding must never stop an owner from seeing whether their own account is connected. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may GET. READ-ONLY PATs MAY NOT CALL THIS: the read is itself the privileged act, so a read-only token is 403 read_only_token in the middleware (changed in spec 1.31.0 — it was permitted before). A full-access PAT or a cookie session reads it normally.

200.description: OK. `configured: false` reports every other field as null.

put.description: Connect (or replace) this store's own Brevo account: exactly api_key, from_address and a nullable from_name — an unknown field is a 400 unknown_field:<name>, never silently ignored. The key is verified against Brevo BEFORE it is stored, on two DISTINCT failures: invalid_api_key (the key itself is rejected — Brevo answers 401/403 on GET /account) and sender_not_verified (the key is fine, but from_address is not one of that account's verified, active senders — the response's message names the address). A transport failure while verifying refuses the save as verification_unavailable (503, safe to retry) rather than storing a key that has never been proven to work. The key is encrypted at rest and NEVER returned by any endpoint — the success body is {"success": true, "configured": true} and nothing more. Returns 503 email_credentials_unavailable while the platform encryption key is not yet configured (checked AFTER body validation, so a malformed body is still reported as its own 400 first). Slice 5c-c: once connected, this account — never a shared platform address — is what emails_enabled's mail actually sends from; see StoreSettings.emails_enabled. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

api_key.description: The store's Brevo API key. Trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace before use; any REMAINING (embedded) control character is a 400. Never echoed back by any response, ever.

from_address.description: Must already be a verified, active sender on that Brevo account — checked against Brevo's own sender list before saving. Containment-checked as an email address at the boundary, not full RFC 5322; the real check is Brevo's.

from_name.description: Optional display name shown in the From header. Defaults to null.

200.description: Stored. The key itself is never echoed back.

400.description: A malformed body — "A JSON object body is required", "api_key must be a string of 1-500 characters", "api_key must not contain control characters", "from_address must be an email address", "from_name must be a string of at most 100 characters", or unknown_field:<name> for any key other than api_key/from_address/from_name — or a Brevo-verified rejection: invalid_api_key (the key itself is wrong) or sender_not_verified (from_address is not a verified sender on that account; `message` names the address).

message.description: Present only for sender_not_verified — names the address that must be verified in Brevo.

503.description: email_credentials_unavailable (platform encryption key not yet configured), store_not_provisioned, or verification_unavailable (Brevo unreachable while verifying — safe to retry)

delete.description: Disconnect this store's Brevo account. No master-key gate here either, following the gateway-credentials precedent: deleting decrypts nothing, so a missing platform secret must never stop a merchant clearing stored credentials. `removed` is false, not an error, when nothing was configured. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

200.description: OK, whether or not anything was configured.

removed.description: Whether a row actually existed to delete.

get.description: What this store's mailer actually did. With `?order_id=N`: every log row for that order, NEWEST FIRST — "did this customer get their receipt". With no parameter: a store-wide summary — "is my mail working at all" — counts by status, the single most recent attempt across all orders (or null if none has ever been made), and up to the 50 most recent failed/skipped attempts, all NEWEST FIRST. `message_id` (Brevo's own id for a sent message) is NEVER returned by either shape — it identifies a message to Brevo support and answers no question an operator has here. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may GET.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: Scope to one order's log rows. Given but malformed (non-integer, zero, or negative) is a 400 — refused, not silently treated as absent.

200.description: OK. Shape depends on whether order_id was given.

oneOf.description: order_id given: this order's own log, newest first.

recent_failures.description: Up to the 50 most recent rows with status failed or skipped, newest first.

get.description: The operator's contact-form inbox (store_form_submissions, store-forms-p2 Tasks 1/6/8/9), NEWEST FIRST, keyset-paged on `id` like /api/v1/reviews (`next_cursor` → `?cursor=`). Unfiltered by default (no implicit `status`). List rows are a lean preview — `fields`/`values` are GET /{id}-only, but `notified_at` rides along here too so the inbox can flag a submission the owner was never emailed about without a second request. `?format=csv` streams EVERY row the filters match, not just the current page — an export capped at the page size would silently hand the owner an incomplete file. The CSV header is `submitted_at,status,form_name` then the union of field keys across the matched rows' fields_snapshot, in first-seen order (never alphabetised, so a form's own field order survives into the spreadsheet). Any cell whose text begins with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is prefixed with a single quote — otherwise Excel/Sheets executes it as a formula the instant the file is opened, a direct path from a filled-in contact form to code running on the owner's machine. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may GET.

parameters.description: Exact match against the form_name snapshotted at submit time.

parameters.name: since

patch.description: The ONLY writable field is `status`. A submission is a record of what someone actually sent — `values`, `fields_snapshot`, `submitter_email` and the timestamps are never writable through this endpoint. Fix round 1: an unknown field is a 400 `unknown_field:<name>`, same convention as `/api/v1/customers/{id}` — never silently ignored, so a client that PATCHes e.g. `values` expecting to rewrite the record is told it didn't, not handed a false 200. A body with no `status` key is a 400 too. Setting `status` to `read` stamps `read_at` the first time only — a later PATCH never moves it. Audited (action `form_submission.status`). Needs a write-capable PAT or a session.

400.description: status missing or not one of new/read/archived, or the body carries a field other than status (unknown_field:<name>).

delete.description: Remove a submission outright. Audited (action `form_submission.delete`).

get.description: List which payment-gateway credentials are configured: provider, mode and timestamps ONLY. This surface is WRITE-ONLY by design — no endpoint ever returns a stored credential (plaintext or ciphertext), and there is no read-back call: an operator who has lost a key re-enters it from the provider’s own dashboard. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; READ-ONLY PATs MAY NOT CALL THIS: the read is itself the privileged act, so a read-only token is 403 read_only_token in the middleware (changed in spec 1.31.0 — it was permitted before). A full-access PAT or a cookie session reads it normally.

put.description: Store (create or replace) the gateway credentials for one provider and mode. The body is the provider’s exact required field set — payplus: api_key, secret_key, payment_page_uid; hyp: user, password; bank_transfer and cash_on_delivery: an empty object {}. Every field is a required non-empty string of at most 500 characters; an unknown field is a 400 unknown_field:<name>, never ignored. Credentials are encrypted at rest and NEVER returned by any endpoint — the success body is {"success": true, "configured": true} and nothing more. Configuring a registered-but-unimplemented provider (hyp) is allowed; taking money through it is refused at checkout until it is implemented. Returns 503 gateway_credentials_unavailable while the platform encryption key is not yet configured. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

get.description: List the store's orders, newest first (placed_at, then id, both descending). All statuses are returned by default — ?status= narrows to one. Paged: ?limit= (default 50, max 100) and ?offset=. Guest orders (customer_id null) are always included alongside account orders. Served by STORE tenants only; read-only tokens may GET. Orders are created by shopper checkout; status transitions are supported via PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id} (order status), PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id}/payments/{paymentId} (offline receipt / release reservation), and POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/refunds (refund reservation). Each order carries its shipping snapshot too — shipping_amount, shipping_label and the six shipping_* address fields (slice 5b-a), plus shipping_method_id (slice 5b-b, the chosen method as an operator-reporting reference; null under the flat rate or once that method is deleted) — which are what the order was charged and where the parcel goes, never the store's current shipping settings; they are absent on orders placed before those columns existed. Response envelope: { data, total, counts }. `total` is data.length for THIS response (page size after filters/limit), not a whole-store row count. `counts` is whole-store and filter-independent — it drives tab labels, not the current page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Omit (or pass all) for every status.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1-100. Anything else is a 400.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Rows to skip. Negative is a 400.

total.description: Always equals data.length — the current page/result-set size, NOT a whole-store COUNT.

counts.description: Whole-store order counts by tab. pending_payment orders are grouped under `unpaid`; other in-flight statuses (processing/completed/refunded) are not part of this tab set.

post.description: Applies one action to many orders rows at once. Every id must belong to THIS store — if ANY id is missing or owned by another store, the WHOLE request is rejected with 400 cross_store_or_missing_ids:<ids> and NOTHING is applied (no partial application of a hostile or stale id list). Idempotent per id — applying the same action twice is a no-op. At most 500 ids per call. mark_shipped sets status=shipped; cancel sets status=cancelled. Served by STORE tenants only; read-only tokens may not POST.

ids.description: store_orders row ids owned by this store.

applied.description: Number of ids the action was applied to — equals ids.length on success (all-or-nothing).

400.description: body must be an object; unknown_action:<action>; ids_required; ids_must_be_positive_integers; too_many_ids (>500); cross_store_or_missing_ids:<ids>

501.description: action: 'export' is accepted but not implemented — no CSV export backend in v1

get.description: One order with its line items, its tax snapshot and its shipping snapshot (shipping_amount, shipping_label, the six shipping_* address fields and shipping_method_id — what was charged for delivery, what the line was called, where it goes, and which method was chosen; never today's settings or a customer's current saved address. Render shipping_label, never a lookup on shipping_method_id, which is null under the flat rate and once the method is deleted). Items render from their purchase-time snapshots (name, unit_price) — later product edits never change them, and the totals are what was charged. Another store's order id is a plain 404. Status transitions are made with PATCH on this same path; recording payment receipt is PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/payments/{paymentId}. The response also carries payments: the payment attempts on the order (id, provider, method_name_snapshot, status, amount, currency, reference, timestamps) — the payments[].id is the paymentId for PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/payments/{paymentId}; an order placed with no payment method has an empty array. The response also carries the derived refundable_amount (see POST /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/refunds), and each payments[] row carries kind (charge | refund | orphan | orphan_refund) and refunds_payment_id (the payment that row refunds, null unless it is a refund) — a refund is its own row; the original charge row is never mutated.

payments.description: Payment rows on this order, oldest first: charges, refunds, orphan and orphan_refund rows, told apart by kind. Each charge row's id is the paymentId for PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/payments/{paymentId}; each orphan row's id is the payment_id for POST /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/refunds. A refund row names what it refunds in refunds_payment_id.

method_name_snapshot.description: The payment method's display name at checkout time — survives the method's deletion.

status.description: Charge rows are 'pending' (checkout wrote it) then 'received' (gateway confirmed) or 'failed' (rejected). Refund reservations are 'pending' then 'received' (provider confirmed) or 'failed' (definitively refused — kept as audit trail, excluded from balance). 'refunded' does not appear on payment rows.

amount.description: Integer minor units, in the order's own currency — server-computed at checkout.

kind.description: What the row IS: 'charge' — money in (every pre-4b row); 'refund' — money out: status 'received' is a confirmed refund, 'pending' is a reservation whose gateway call has not concluded (it still holds its amount against refundable_amount — if it persists, the refund crashed mid-flight and needs reconciling with the gateway), 'failed' is a refused attempt kept as audit trail that holds nothing; 'orphan' — verified money that arrived for an already-settled order, recorded for reconciliation and never counted toward refundable_amount; 'orphan_refund' — that orphan money going back out, with the same pending/received/failed meanings as a refund row, against the orphan's own balance.

refunds_payment_id.description: The id of the payment row THIS row refunds: the settled charge for a 'refund' row, the orphan row for an 'orphan_refund' row. Null on charge and orphan rows (they refund nothing), and null on a refund recorded before this field existed — such a row cannot be attributed to a single orphan, so this endpoint's per-row orphan refunds are refused on that order until it is resolved in the provider's dashboard. The outstanding amount of one orphan row is its amount minus the non-failed 'orphan_refund' rows naming it.

notes.description: Optional operator-supplied audit note on this payment row (Phase A, migration 0078). Plain text, at most 2000 characters, no control characters. Null when no note was recorded.

patch.description: Move the order through its lifecycle: body is exactly {status} — one of processing, shipped, completed, cancelled, refunded. Legal moves: pending_payment → cancelled; paid → processing | cancelled | refunded; processing → shipped | cancelled | refunded; shipped → completed | refunded (cancel is unavailable once shipped — the goods are gone, refund is the path); completed → refunded; cancelled → refunded; refunded is terminal. An illegal move is a 409 and changes nothing. 'refunded' has one extra gate: an order whose settled charge was taken by an online gateway (payplus) cannot be marked refunded until refund rows the gateway confirmed cover the captured amount — this endpoint never contacts the gateway, so marking such an order refunded by hand would record a refund whose money never moved; it is a 409 pointing at POST /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/refunds, which actually sends the money back (a full refund through it transitions the order automatically). A pending refund reservation does not open the gate — only confirmed ('received') refunds count. Offline charges are unaffected: refunding a bank transfer out-of-band and recording it here is exactly what the move is for. 'paid' is NEVER settable here — recording payment receipt (PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/payments/{paymentId}) is the only route to paid, and asking for it is a 409. Both cancelled and refunded return each line's quantity to its product's stock, exactly once per order — the ordinary cancelled → refunded sequence does not restock twice, and the order's restocked_at records when stock came back. Only TRACKED products are touched: an untracked product (stock null) stays untracked, nothing is written to it. Refunding restocks even when the goods were not returned: for a tracked product, correct its stock field afterwards if they weren't — never by writing a number onto an untracked product, which would silently turn tracking on. If the order's status changed concurrently between read and write, the call is a 409 and changes nothing — re-read and retry. An unknown body field is a 400 unknown_field:<name>, never silently ignored. Another store's order id, an unknown id or a malformed id is a plain 404. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

status.description: The target status. 'paid' and 'pending_payment' are not settable here: paid is reached only by recording payment receipt, and nothing returns to pending_payment.

200.description: OK — the order is in the requested status; if it was cancelled or refunded and had not been restocked before, its line quantities are back in stock

400.description: Validation failed: the body was not a JSON object, status was missing or not a known order status, or an unknown field was sent (unknown_field:<name>)

409.description: The move is not legal from the order's current status (Cannot transition <from> -> <to>), status was 'paid' — which only recording payment receipt can set — the order's money sits with an online gateway (payplus) and confirmed refunds do not yet cover the captured amount — use POST /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/refunds to actually send the money back — or the order's status changed concurrently while the transition was processing (nothing happened; re-read and retry)

post.description: Record an additional payment on an existing order (operator-initiated split-tender). Writes a new kind='charge' row on the order. Offline providers only (bank_transfer, cash_on_delivery) — a gateway provider is refused with 400 because its status can only reach 'received' via callback, not operator POST. The order must not be cancelled or refunded. Body: { method_id, amount, status?, reference?, notes? }. method_id must name an enabled offline payment method belonging to this store. amount is a positive integer in minor units; it must not push the sum of received charges past order.total (overpay guard). status defaults to 'pending'; 'received' is the fast path for recording a payment that already arrived, skipping the create-then-PATCH dance. status='received' requires a reference (the bank/dashboard record of what arrived, at most 200 characters plain text). notes is optional plain text, at most 2000 characters, no control characters. Returns { success: true, id: <new payment id>, order_status: <order status after write> } — order_status is included because a received receipt that covers the outstanding balance transitions the order pending_payment → paid in the same batch. Served by STORE tenants only; authenticated with a store PAT.

method_id.description: Id of an enabled offline payment method belonging to this store. Gateway providers (payplus, hyp) are refused with 400.

amount.description: Positive integer minor units. Must not push the sum of received charges past order.total.

status.description: Default 'pending'. 'received' is the fast path for an offline receipt that already arrived; requires reference.

reference.description: Plain text, at most 200 characters. Required when status='received' (the bank/dashboard record of what arrived). Optional otherwise.

notes.description: Optional operator audit note. Plain text, at most 2000 characters, no control characters.

id.description: Id of the newly created payment row.

order_status.description: Order status after the write. A received receipt that covers the outstanding balance transitions the order pending_payment → paid in the same batch.

400.description: Validation failed — missing or invalid method_id/amount, gateway provider, overpay, status='received' without reference, unknown field, or non-JSON-object body

409.description: Order is cancelled or refunded — new payments cannot be recorded on it

patch.description: Record that the money for an OFFLINE payment arrived: the payment goes 'received' and the order goes pending_payment → paid. Offline only — a payment made through an online gateway (payplus) is refused with 409 and nothing is written: such a payment is settled solely by the tenant's own server-side verification of the gateway transaction, and its reference holds the gateway's transaction id, which that verification reads. On a charge row it accepts ONLY status: 'received'. The one other operation this endpoint offers is releasing a STRANDED REFUND RESERVATION: a row with kind 'refund' or 'orphan_refund' and status 'pending' (left when a crash or timeout interrupted a refund between reserving and confirming) blocks all further refunds of its own balance on the order until an operator, having checked the provider's dashboard, resolves it — status 'failed' records that the money never moved (the reservation is released and the refundable balance returns; a reference is refused, there is nothing to reference), or status 'received' with the provider's own REFUND reference (required) records that it did move. Only a pending refund or orphan_refund row can be released (anything else is a 409), a reference already recorded on another payment is a 409 (the usual mistake is pasting the charge's transaction uid instead of the refund's), and the release never moves the ORDER's status — once confirmed refunds cover the capture, PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id} marks the order refunded and restocks. An orphan payment (kind 'orphan') is never mutated here: its money is refunded, or its out-of-band return recorded, through POST /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/refunds with payment_id, which writes an orphan_refund row and leaves the orphan row 'received' as the durable record of what arrived; status 'refunded' is a 400 on every row. Other ORDER status transitions are made with PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id}, but this call remains the only route to paid. Idempotent: repeating the call returns 200, and an order that has already moved past pending_payment (e.g. shipped) is never dragged back to paid — only the payment row updates. Recording receipt on a cancelled or refunded order is a 409 — the money already left, and a received payment on a dead order would be a silent contradiction; recording receipt on an online gateway payment is a 409 whatever the order's status. An unknown body field is rejected with 400 unknown_field:<name>, never silently ignored, and a reference over 200 characters is a 400, never truncated. The payment must belong to the order in the URL and to this store; any mismatch, unknown id or malformed id is a plain 404. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

status.description: 'received' records offline money arriving on a charge row, or — on a pending kind='refund' or kind='orphan_refund' row, with the provider's refund reference — that a stranded refund did go through. 'failed' is valid ONLY for releasing a pending kind='refund' or kind='orphan_refund' row (the money never moved); on any other row it is a 400. 'refunded' is never settable — orphan money is refunded through POST /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/refunds with payment_id.

reference.description: Optional operator note identifying the money (e.g. a bank transfer reference). Plain text — control bytes and angle brackets are rejected, and anything over 200 characters is a 400, never truncated. Omit to keep a previously stored reference; null or blank clears it. When releasing a pending refund reservation as 'received' the reference is REQUIRED and must be the provider's own refund reference; a reference sent with a 'failed' release is a 400.

200.description: OK — the payment is recorded as received and the order is paid (or was already past pending_payment)

400.description: Validation failed: status was not 'received' or 'failed', 'failed' was sent for a row that is not a pending refund reservation, a 'received' release of a refund reservation came without the provider's refund reference (or a 'failed' one came with a reference), the reference was not plain text or exceeded 200 characters (rejected, never truncated), an unknown field was sent (unknown_field:<name>), or the body was not a JSON object

404.description: No such payment on this order

409.description: Receipt cannot be recorded: the order is cancelled or refunded (the money already left), or the payment was made through an online gateway (payplus) and is settled only by the tenant's server-side verification of the gateway transaction, never by hand, the refund row addressed is not a pending reservation (already resolved — settled money records do not flip), or the reference is already recorded on another payment (enter the refund's own uid, not the charge's)

post.description: Revert a payment back to 'reverted' status (undo an accidental 'mark received'). Distinct from a refund — a revert says 'this payment did not happen' and leaves an audit trail; no money moves. Offline providers only (bank_transfer, cash_on_delivery); gateway payments are refused with 400. Only a 'received' charge row is revertable — a 'pending' row has not arrived yet and is refused with 409. If the revert drops the sum of received charges below the order total on a 'paid' order, the order also transitions back to 'pending_payment' in the same batch. post.description: Refund a settled gateway (payplus) charge back to the shopper — the one operation that moves money OUT. Body {amount} in integer minor units for a partial refund, or an empty object {} to refund the full remaining balance. The refundable balance is DERIVED server-side (captured charge minus prior non-failed refund rows — the order's refundable_amount); an amount exceeding it is a 400 and the payment provider is never contacted. The refund row is RESERVED (kind 'refund', status 'pending') under that balance atomically BEFORE the gateway is called, so two concurrent refunds can never together exceed the captured amount — the loser is a 409 and never reaches the gateway. On gateway success the row is confirmed 'received' with the provider's refund uid as its reference; on a DEFINITIVE gateway refusal (it processed the request and did not pay) it is marked 'failed' (502) — an audit row that releases the balance and counts toward nothing. An AMBIGUOUS gateway failure does NOT release it: a 5xx, a timed-out or rejected call, or a refunded amount that came back different from the one requested all leave the row 'pending' (502), because in those states nobody knows whether the money moved. A reservation left 'pending' — that case, a crash mid-refund, or a 500 from this call after the gateway confirmed — keeps holding its amount and blocks further refunds until it is reconciled with the provider and released with PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/payments/{paymentId}. Money is server-computed throughout: currency and captured amount come from the charge row, never the request. A PARTIAL refund leaves the order's status untouched (still a paid order) and restocks nothing; when the refunded total reaches the captured amount the order transitions to refunded through the ordinary state machine — judged at write time, so an order moved (e.g. to processing) while the gateway call was in flight still transitions — and TRACKED stock returns exactly once, same as PATCH {status: refunded}. A 409 also answers an order that is already fully refunded, has no settled payment, or whose charge was taken offline (bank_transfer, cash_on_delivery — refund those out-of-band, then move the order with PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id}). ORPHAN money — a kind 'orphan' payment row, the verified extra charge recorded when a second payment arrived on an already-settled order — is refunded through this same endpoint by naming the row: body {payment_id} (optionally with {amount} for a partial refund; omitted, the full outstanding amount capped at that row's amount). The orphan refund has its OWN balance, fully separate from the charge's, and that balance is PER ROW: what one orphan row still holds is its own amount minus the non-failed kind 'orphan_refund' rows that name it (refunds_payment_id), so each orphan on an order is refundable exactly once and only up to what it took. Orphan activity never changes refundable_amount in either direction — refunding the accidental second payment can never consume the shopper's right to a refund of the first. The gateway is called against the ORPHAN row's own transaction uid, the same reserve-first guard and definitive-vs-ambiguous handling apply (the reservation and result rows carry kind 'orphan_refund'), a stranded pending orphan_refund row blocks further orphan refunds until released with the payments PATCH, and an orphan refund NEVER moves the order's status — it is not a lifecycle event on the sale. Body {payment_id, reference} instead records an out-of-band return the operator already made in the provider's dashboard: an orphan_refund row lands 'received' with that reference under the same balance guard, the provider is not called, and the orphan row itself is never mutated. reference without payment_id is a 400 (a charge refund always goes through the gateway); a reference already recorded on another payment is a 409 (don't paste the charge's transaction uid); payment_id naming anything but a received orphan row of this order is a 400/409, an unknown payment_id a plain 404. An order holding more than one received orphan is refunded row by row, each against its own balance. The one case still refused with a 409 is an order carrying a non-failed orphan_refund row whose refunds_payment_id is null (only a refund recorded before that field existed): nothing can say which orphan it returned, so no orphan on that order may be targeted — resolve it in the provider's dashboard. An out-of-band record is FINAL: it consumes the outstanding orphan balance and cannot be undone or released. A 200 for an orphan refund returns orphan_outstanding in place of refundable_amount: the ORDER's outstanding orphan money after this refund — the sum of every received orphan row's own remaining amount. An unknown body field is a 400 unknown_field:<name>, never silently ignored. Another store's order id, an unknown id or a malformed id is a plain 404. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

get.description:
The operator's data-subject-request register: what was asked, of what kind, when it arrived, when it is due, which rule set that deadline, and how many days are left. Admin only; read-only tokens may GET. SOONEST DUE FIRST — `ORDER BY due_at IS NULL, due_at ASC, id ASC`: known deadlines in the order they fall due, then the rows whose deadline nobody could establish, because unknown is not more urgent than due on Friday. This is a work queue with a legal clock, so the most urgent request is on the FIRST page and never the last; do not re-sort a page client-side, which would look ordered while hiding the rows that matter. Paged with `?limit=N&offset=M` — take `next_offset` from one response and send it back as `?offset=` for the next page; it is null on the last page.

THIS ENDPOINT FULFILS NOTHING, and `fulfilment` says so in every response. Listing a request is not answering it: generating an export and running the erasure cascade are a later phase. An operator who reads this list and does nothing has not satisfied anything on it.

`days_remaining` and `overdue` are COMPUTED AT READ TIME and are not columns. A null `due_at` means the deadline is UNKNOWN — no rule resolved for that requester, or the tenant was mid-upgrade at intake — and `days_remaining` and `overdue` are null alongside it rather than 0 and false. No default period is substituted anywhere.

The register holds NO request body, NO e-mail address and NO IP, so none is returned: a DSAR's substance is the shopper's own words and stays in the mailbox the operator already has. The salted subject pseudonym and the unverified-requester token hash are columns but are never serialised.

503 `privacy_requests_unavailable` during the upgrade window before the register's migration lands — an empty list would read as "nobody has asked for anything".

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Non-numeric or 0 falls back to 50; above 200 is capped, below 1 raised to 1.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Rows to skip — the previous page's `next_offset`. Given but not a non-negative integer is a 400, refused rather than silently restarted from the top: on this list the first page is the one holding the deadlines about to breach. Page two keys off the same ORDER BY as page one, so no row is repeated or skipped, and a newly received request sorts to the END of the order (its deadline is the furthest away) rather than shifting rows out from under a caller.

NULL means no deadline rule resolved for this requester (or the tenant was mid-upgrade when the request arrived): the deadline is UNKNOWN. No default is substituted anywhere — a number here always came off a rule.

deadline_rule.description: `<jurisdiction>/<rule key>:<version>` — which rule produced due_at, e.g. EU/gdpr.response.deadline:1. Null exactly when due_at is.

days_remaining.description: COMPUTED AT READ TIME from due_at and now, never stored — a persisted countdown is wrong the moment nobody looks at it. Negative when the deadline has passed. NULL when due_at is null.

overdue.description: true when now is past due_at. NULL — not false — when due_at is null: false would assert the request is inside a deadline nobody has established.

outcome_note.description: The operator's note on the outcome, e.g. open_orders when the erasure flow refused.

routed_to.description: Which existing flow the request was handed to: deletion_request, consent_withdrawal, account_profile. Null for access and portability, which are tracked here and fulfilled later.

next_offset.description: The offset to send as `?offset=` for the next page; null on the final page.

fulfilment.description: Always "none". Stated in the payload so no client can build a screen on the assumption that a row here is a request being handled.

patch.description:
Record something against a register row. Admin only; a write, so a read-only token is refused and a session must carry X-CSRF-Token.

AN EXTENSION IS RECORDED, NEVER TAKEN. `{ extension_reason }` stamps `extension_claimed_at` and stores the reason, and LEAVES `due_at` AND `deadline_rule` EXACTLY AS THE INTAKE COMPUTED THEM. The GDPR's further two months are conditional on telling the data subject inside the first month WITH REASONS, and the Israeli further 15 days are granted by the head of the Authority — neither is something a shop may assume, so neither is applied here. A claim is the operator's record that they claimed one; it buys the store no time in this API, and nothing in this codebase moves a deadline. `due_at`, `deadline_rule`, `received_at`, `kind` and `customer_id` are not writable by any spelling: an unknown field is a 400, not an ignored key.

A claim is WRITE-ONCE: a second one is 409 `extension_already_claimed`, because `extension_claimed_at` is the date the notification obligation is measured against and overwriting it would erase the evidence. An extension with a blank reason is 400 `extension_reason_required`.

`{ status, outcome_note? }` records the OUTCOME the operator reached: answered, refused or withdrawn only, stamping `answered_at`. The intake states (open, verifying, routed) are not hand-writable, and nothing in this phase marks a request answered on its own.

Both writes are audited as `privacy_request.extension` / `privacy_request.outcome` with the request id and kind — never the subject, never any contents.
