503.description: This store is mid-upgrade and the column this write needs does not exist yet

post.description: Applies one action to many products rows at once. Every id must belong to THIS store — if ANY id is missing or owned by another store, the WHOLE request is rejected with 400 cross_store_or_missing_ids:<ids> and NOTHING is applied (no partial application of a hostile or stale id list). Idempotent per id — applying the same action twice is a no-op. At most 500 ids per call. enable/disable set visible=1/0; delete removes the row; add_category/remove_category (with category_id) write the join table. Served by STORE tenants only; read-only tokens may not POST.

ids.description: store_products row ids owned by this store.

category_id.description: Required with add_category / remove_category: the category to add the products to (idempotent) or take them out of. 404 category_not_found; 409 category_is_smart — an automatic category's rules decide its membership.

tag.description: Required with add_tag / remove_tag: the tag name (add_tag creates it if new).

applied.description: Number of ids the action was applied to — equals ids.length on success (all-or-nothing).

400.description: body must be an object; unknown_action:<action>; ids_required; ids_must_be_positive_integers; too_many_ids (>500); cross_store_or_missing_ids:<ids>

501.description: action: 'export' is accepted but not implemented — no CSV export backend in v1

get.description: The store's most recent import jobs, newest first (up to 25). Store tenants only. Read-only tokens may GET. Each job carries `pending_rows`: how many of its staged rows are still to process. /run is deliberately call-again-until-done because a tenant Worker has no queue or alarm, so a job whose client stopped calling sits with rows untouched and nothing advances it - `pending_rows` greater than 0 is how a caller tells that apart from a finished job, and the state name alone cannot.

pending_rows.description: Staged rows still in state pending for this job. Greater than 0 means the import is unfinished whatever its state name says.

post.description: Create an import job in the `staging` state. The FILE itself never reaches this endpoint - the admin parses csv/json/xml client-side and posts normalised rows separately via `POST /api/v1/products/import/{id}/rows`. `mapping` and `options` are opaque column-mapping/config objects the admin round-trips; each must serialise to at most 64KB. `total_rows` is the count the admin's own parse produced and is later checked (never overwritten) against what actually arrives before the job can leave staging. Write tokens only.

options.description: At most 64KB serialised. Defaults to {}. `download_images: false` skips fetching remote images during run (see /run).

400.description: Invalid JSON body, format not csv/json/xml, filename over 255 characters, total_rows not a whole number in 1..100000, or mapping/options not a plain object or over 64KB serialised.

get.description: A generated (not static) sample file for `?format=csv|json|xml` (default csv), pre-filled with this store's own currency, real category/tag names where the store has them, and prices written in MAJOR units the way an operator types them (e.g. '24.99'), matching what the importer accepts field-for-field. The response is the file itself, not a JSON envelope - `content-type` matches the format and `content-disposition` is `attachment`. Store tenants only. Read-only tokens may GET.

200.description: The sample file, as an attachment.

400.description: format must be csv, json or xml.

post.description: Connect a catalogue source (Shopify public, Shopify Admin, or WooCommerce) and verify it BEFORE any row is created: the address is coerced through the same check the image fetcher uses, one real page is fetched, and only then is a source row written. Credentials are sealed with a per-tenant key and are never returned. Two daily ceilings apply and are deliberately separate: distinct hosts connected today, and total connection ATTEMPTS today (a failed verify still costs an attempt, which is what bounds outbound fetches). The counter row is written BEFORE the fetch, and a failure to write it is a 503 rather than an unmetered fetch. A store answering with a web page instead of product data reports that it is blocked and suggests the access-token option.

base_url.description: The store address. A myshopify.com address for Shopify, not a public storefront domain.

secret.description: Admin API access token, or WooCommerce consumer key and secret. Sealed at rest; never returned.

attested.description: Required for the public-catalogue path: the operator confirms they own or administer the store.

get.description: List this store’s connected catalogue sources. Sealed credentials are never included.

delete.description: Forget a connected source and its sealed credentials. This does NOT reset the daily connection ceilings: those are counted per store per day, so deleting a source cannot be used to buy more attempts. An id belonging to another store returns 404, not 403.

get.description: The job's state plus per-row counts and up to 200 failed rows (idx, error, payload). `job.mapping` and `job.options` come back parsed, not as JSON strings. A job belonging to another store is a 404, never a 403 - the store's no-leak rule is that an unauthorised id is indistinguishable from a missing one. Store tenants only. Read-only tokens may GET.

failures.description: Up to 200 failed rows, ordered by idx.

404.description: No such import job in this store (also an invalid id) - never distinguished from an unauthorised id.

post.description: Pull ONE page of products from the connected source into this job’s staged rows, then return. Like /run, nothing advances a job except the client calling this again: **call it repeatedly while `done` is false.** One page per call keeps a tenant Worker inside its CPU budget. The cursor is written AFTER the rows it produced, so an interrupted pull resumes without losing or duplicating a page, and rows are deduplicated on the source product id. If the source asks us to slow down, the response carries a retry hint rather than failing. Three consecutive failures pause the job instead of hammering the source, and the sealed credentials are deleted once the pull reports done.

Close staging and move the job to `ready`, the state /run requires. The row count staged so far is checked against the job's own recorded `total_rows` (set at creation, never against the `total_rows` in this call's body) - a short-staged import is refused rather than silently importing part of a file. Only valid while the job is `staging`. Write tokens only.

total_rows.description: Informational only; the check is against the job's own recorded total_rows, not this value.

400.description: total_rows is missing or not a positive whole number, or fewer rows have been staged than the job's recorded total_rows.

404.description: No such import job in this store (also an invalid id) - never distinguished from an unauthorised id.

409.description: The job has already left staging (state is ready, running, paused or done).

post.description: Stage one SECTION of the parsed file - at most 500 rows per call, so a 10,000-row file is sent in sections rather than one enormous body. Idempotent on `(job_id, idx)`: re-sending a section (e.g. after a client timeout) replaces the same rows rather than duplicating them, and a resent idx does not count twice against the job's 100,000-row ceiling. Only valid while the job is `staging`. Write tokens only.

idx.description: The row's 1-based position in the original file. Not an array index - used as the idempotency key with job_id.

payload.description: The normalised product fields for this row (a subset of IMPORT_FIELDS, plus optional categories/tags/images), as the admin's mapper produced them.

total.description: Rows staged on the job so far, across all calls.

400.description: rows is missing or not an array, more than 500 rows in one call, a row's idx is not a positive whole number, a row's payload is not an object, or staging these rows would push the job over its 100,000-row ceiling.

404.description: No such import job in this store (also an invalid id) - never distinguished from an unauthorised id.

409.description: The job has already left staging (state is ready, running, paused or done) - rows can only be added while it is staging.

post.description: Process ONE bounded batch (25 product rows, or up to 25 images' worth of one image phase) and return. This is also the resume button: a tenant Worker has no queue or alarm, so nothing advances a job except the client calling this again. **Call it repeatedly while the response's `remaining` is greater than 0 - this is not a fire-and-forget endpoint.** A single call does either the products phase or the images phase, never both. If another call currently holds the job's lease (near-simultaneous polling is expected), the response is `{ busy: true, phase: 'busy', remaining, ... }` with everything else zeroed - **this is not an error and not completion; wait briefly and call again.** Calling run on an already-`done` job is a no-op that returns zeroed counts with `remaining: 0`, so a client's own last poll racing the finish never surfaces as a failure. Only valid once the job has left `staging` (i.e. after /ready). Write tokens only.

remaining.description: Rows still pending or in-progress. Keep calling /run while this is above 0.

busy.description: Present and true only when another call held the lease and no work was done this call.

results.description: Per-row outcomes for this call's batch only. Empty when phase is 'busy' or 'done'.

image_errors.description: Images phase only: how many of this row's image URLs failed. An image failure never fails the row - the product still exists.

404.description: No such import job in this store (also an invalid id) - never distinguished from an unauthorised id.

409.description: The job is still staging - it has not been marked ready yet.

get.description: List this store's URL-preservation redirects (project 4), newest first. Keyset-paginated: ?limit=N&before=<id>; next_before is the last id on this page when more rows exist below it, null on the final page. ?state=pending|live and ?source=<source> filter. `state` explains itself in the row: pending means the destination does not resolve yet and this answers a non-cached 302; live means the engine has confirmed the destination and this answers a cacheable 301. Read-only tokens may GET.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Keyset cursor: only rows with id < this.

post.description: Add one redirect by hand. from_path is normalised with the engine's own rule (lowercased, query/hash stripped, trailing slash and repeated slashes collapsed) before it is stored, so it always matches what a shopper's request normalises to at read time. Refused with 400 if from_path already names a live page route (/, /products, /cart, /checkout, /search, /account/*, /pages/*, and the rest of _middleware.js's page-route set) - a row there can never fire. to_path must be an internal path starting with a single / (never a scheme, never protocol-relative //host). Always created state: pending and source: operator - only the engine itself (on lookup) ever flips a row to live, and an operator-added row is never attributed to a migration import so it cannot be swept up by a wholesale DELETE ?source=migration:... afterwards. 409 if a redirect from this path already exists.

400.description: Missing/invalid from_path or to_path, or from_path names a live page route.

409.description: A redirect from this path already exists.

delete.description: Undo a whole import at once: deletes every redirect row stamped with the given ?source (required) - operator says undo, every row migration:backfill (or migration:shopify, migration:woocommerce) created comes out together. Does not touch rows from any other source. There is no unfiltered DELETE on this collection by design.

200.description: Rows deleted (0 is a normal answer - that source had nothing to undo).

post.description: Create redirect rows for products and categories this store already migrated (store_products.source_handle / store_categories.source_handle, set by the catalogue migration, NULL for anything not migrated). Bounded per call, like the product-import endpoints: processes up to 500 candidate products and 500 candidate categories and returns; call again while done is false. A product is skipped (and counted in products.skipped_same_slug) when source_handle equals its slug - /products/<handle> already resolves via the engine's own pattern, so a row would be dead weight. Categories always get a row when migrated (/collections/<handle> -> /categories/<slug>) because the engine has no pattern for that shape at all - categories were built from product_type names, not collection handles. Every row is created source: migration:backfill, state: pending. Safe to call repeatedly: re-running inserts nothing a previous call already created (UNIQUE(store_id, from_path), INSERT OR IGNORE).

skipped_same_slug.description: Whole-store count, not just this batch - a reassuring number, not a failure: most migrated products need no row at all.

done.description: True once both products.remaining and categories.remaining are 0. Call this endpoint again while false.

delete.description: Remove one redirect row. An id belonging to another store (or no row at all) returns 404, not 403 - store_id scoping is the only intra-tenant boundary here and it has no crypto behind it.

404.description: No redirect with this id for this store.

get.description: Fetch one product, any status. The row includes `categories`: the array of category ids the product belongs to. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET. Also includes `options` (the product's option names) and `variants` (see /api/v1/products/{id}/variants) — empty for a product without variants. Also primary_category_id.

patch.description: Partial update; send only the fields to change. Sending `categories` REPLACES the product’s category membership in one transaction — it is not merged, so an empty array clears it. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET. RULE: a write that sets status active, or rewrites categories, may not leave an active product with no category (400) — membership held by a smart category counts. Changing `slug` records the previous one as rename history: the old URL then 301s to the new one, and any migration redirect that pointed at the old slug is repointed, so inbound links stay at one hop.

slug.description: Defaults to a slug derived from name. Must be unique across the store.

price.description: Non-negative integer minor units (1999 = 19.99). Floats and negatives are rejected with 400, never rounded.

compare_at_price.description: Non-negative integer minor units, or null.

currency.description: 3-letter uppercase ISO 4217 code. Anything else is a 400. Defaults to the owning store’s currency when omitted on create.

images.description: Array of image URLs (or a pre-encoded JSON string).

stock.description: Units in stock, or null for NOT TRACKED (the default; untracked products are never refused at checkout). Setting null turns tracking off. A negative or non-integer value is a 400. Checkout decrements tracked stock; cancelling or refunding an order returns it. SETTLES ANY DEBT: the value you send is the units you now have, so anything already `backordered` comes off the top before the rest becomes available — sending 20 against a debt of 3 stores stock 17 and backordered 0, and sending null clears the debt with the tracking. `stock` and `backordered` are therefore never both positive.

shipping_exempt.description: never adds a delivery charge; free_over is judged on the non-exempt goods; an all-exempt cart records shipping_amount 0. Also accepts true/false. 503 while the store is finishing the upgrade that adds the column (a 0 is dropped on PATCH).

allow_oversell.description: Per-product permission to sell past stock (default 0 — every product behaves as it always has). With it set, checkout no longer refuses this product for insufficient stock: stock floors at 0 and each unit sold past it is added to backordered instead. It does NOT weaken the stock guard for any other product.

backorder_notice.description: Operator-authored copy shown to shoppers on the product page and in the cart while this product is flagged AND out of stock. null (the default) means the shopper is told NOTHING — a deliberate choice, never filled in with a default. Escaped server-side, like a payment method's instructions.

categories.description: Category ids. On PATCH this REPLACES the product’s membership (an empty array removes it from every category); omit the field to leave membership unchanged. An unknown id is a 400 and nothing is written.

supplier_id.description: Must name a supplier belonging to this store (400 otherwise), or null. Defaults to null on create.

cost_price.description: OPERATOR-ONLY. Integer minor units, non-negative, or null for UNKNOWN (never zero). Defaults to null on create. Never rendered on any shopper-facing surface.

supplier_external_id.description: An AliExpress item URL or bare item id; parsed and stored as the bare id. Requires supplier_id to already be set (on this same write or already on the row) — 400 otherwise. null clears it. OPERATOR-ONLY; never rendered on any shopper-facing surface. Labels sourcing only, by itself — POST /api/v1/suppliers/{supplierId}/sync is the endpoint that actually pulls cost and stock from AliExpress for a product carrying this field.

primary_category_id.description: Must be one of `categories` (POST) or of the product's categories after the write (PATCH) — 400 otherwise. May be sent alone on PATCH to change only the primary. A membership rewrite that omits it keeps the current primary while it is still a member. 503 on a tenant still receiving the migration.

custom_fields.description: REPLACES the product's detail fields (send the whole object; null or {} clears). Empty-string/null values drop out. Keys: 1-40 chars of a-z 0-9 _; strings ≤2000 chars. 503 on a tenant still receiving the migration.

tags.description: REPLACES the product's tags (names; a tag is created the first time any product names it, matched by slug so 'Gift idea' and 'gift-idea' are one tag). null or [] clears. Omit to keep.

tax_class_id.description: One of this store's tax classes, or null for standard. Another store's id, an unknown id or a non-integer is a 400 invalid_tax_class; a real id while the store is still finishing migration 0210 is a 503.

400.description: Invalid field values (price must be a non-negative integer in minor units; a categories id must name an existing category; supplier_external_id is not a string / is not a parseable AliExpress item URL or id; supplier_external_id is set without a supplier_id; or clearing supplier_id would orphan an existing supplier_external_id without clearing it too)

409.description: A product with this slug already exists

503.description: The store is mid-upgrade and the oversell columns do not exist yet, and this request asked for nothing else. Retry shortly. Never returned once migrations 0034-0036 have run.

delete.description: Delete a product. Its category-membership rows are removed with it; categories themselves are untouched. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

get.description: List the product's images ordered by sort_order. Store tenants only. Read-only tokens may GET.

404.description: No such product in this store (also an invalid id).

post.description: Upload one or more image files (multipart field `files[]`). Every file is MIME-checked before any work; a single non-image refuses the whole batch with 400. Each accepted file is transcoded to three AVIF variants (thumb/medium/large) and stored in the store's R2 bucket; the first image on the product becomes primary. Per-file failures do not abort the batch: the response is 207 with `success: false` and the failed entries carry `id: null` plus `error`/`detail`. Requires the IMAGE_PROCESSOR and STORE_MEDIA_R2 bindings (503 otherwise). Write tokens only.

207.description: At least one file failed; the others were stored

400.description: Not multipart, no files[], or a file that is not an image (`error` is the operator-facing sentence, `detail` the technical reason).

404.description: No such product in this store (also an invalid id).

503.description: Store not provisioned, or the tenant worker lacks the IMAGE_PROCESSOR / STORE_MEDIA_R2 binding and needs a re-upgrade.

post.description: Bulk sort_order update: `order` is the full list of the product's image ids in the desired order (sort_order becomes the array index). The set must match the product's current image ids exactly — a missing, extra or foreign id refuses the whole request with 400. Write tokens only.

400.description: Invalid JSON, empty order, or an id set that is not exactly the product's image ids.

404.description: No such product in this store (also an invalid id).

post.description: Attach an external image by URL — nothing is fetched or transcoded, the URL is stored verbatim. `url` must start with http://, https:// or a single `/` (protocol-relative `//` is refused) and be at most 2000 characters. `alt_text` defaults to an auto-generated one from the product name. The first image on the product becomes primary. Write tokens only.

400.description: Invalid JSON, unsafe url scheme, or url over 2000 characters.

404.description: No such product in this store (also an invalid id).

patch.description: Edit alt_text, sort_order and/or is_primary. Setting is_primary: 1 demotes the current primary in the same batch, so the product always has exactly one. At least one field is required. Write tokens only.

400.description: Invalid JSON, a wrong-typed field, or no fields to update.

404.description: No such product, or no such image on this product.

delete.description: Delete the image row; for `upload` rows the three R2 variants are removed best-effort. Deleting the primary promotes the remaining image with the lowest sort_order. Write tokens only.

404.description: No such product, or no such image on this product.

get.description: The product's variants and option names. Empty on a product without variants. Read-only tokens may GET.

put.description: REPLACE the product's variants. `options` are the option names (up to 3); every variant gives a value for each. Rows with an `id` are updated, rows without are created, variants missing from the body are deleted (their cart lines go with them; order lines keep their snapshots). Name, slug, currency, status, visibility and type derive from the parent — PATCHing the parent's name/status re-derives them. The storefront then lists the parent "From" its cheapest variant, and its product page offers the pickers; a variant's own slug redirects to the parent. 503 on a tenant still finishing the upgrade that adds the columns.

id.description: An existing variant of this product, to update.

400.description: Validation: option names, a repeated combination, money, stock, or an id that is not this product's variant.

get.description: The operator's review moderation queue, NEWEST FIRST, keyset-paged on `id` like /api/v1/audit-log (`next_before` → `?before=`). `status` defaults to `pending`; pass `all` for everything. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may GET. Backs /admin/reviews.

patch.description: Moderate one review: `approved` shows it on the product page and counts it toward the rating; `rejected` hides it; `pending` sends it back to the queue. Audited (action `review.status`). Needs a write-capable PAT or a session.

delete.description: Remove a review outright (spam). Audited (action `review.delete`).

get.description: v1 STUB. The admin top-bar search input renders and submits against this endpoint, but cross-resource search (products + orders + customers) is not implemented yet — this always returns an empty result set with stub: true and an X-Feature-Status: stub response header, never a 404, so the frontend can render "no results" without a special-case error path. Served by STORE tenants only.

Read the store's settings: the 21 fields of StoreSettings, exactly — identity, contact, currency/locale/timezone, tax, shipping, email and analytics. The tax fields (tax_enabled, tax_rate, tax_inclusive), the shipping fields (shipping_enabled, shipping_flat_amount, tax_shipping), emails_enabled and email_log_retention_days are LIVE — checkout applies the tax and shipping fields and snapshots the result onto the order, and, while emails_enabled is 1, emails the shopper an order confirmation and, when the store has an email set, the operator a new-order alert; the same switch also sends the shopper a payment-confirmed email when the order reaches `paid` and a status email on every subsequent transition (processing, shipped, completed, cancelled, refunded). Slice 5c-c: emails_enabled alone is not enough — mail also requires a connected Brevo account (`PUT /api/v1/email-credentials`); a store without one sends nothing. Slice 5c-d adds a fifth mail kind, refund_confirmed, sent by a call that causes NO status transition: when a stranded refund reservation confirms and its confirmed total now completes coverage of the capture, it corrects a refunded figure that status_refunded quoted too low, sent at most once per order. email_log_retention_days (default 90, 0 = keep forever) controls how long store_email_log rows survive — checked once per send batch, but nothing is actually pruned until migration 0061 has run against a given tenant's database. Only the analytics ids (google_analytics_id, facebook_pixel_id) are stored without being applied: the storefront emits them in slice 6, so do not report those as live behaviour. Served by STORE tenants with store data. On a CMS tenant the SAME path exists too: the CMS’s own /api/v1 mirror routes it to a different CMS resource, so a 200 here does not prove you are talking to a store — check GET /api/v1/users/me, whose `product` field names the product that answered. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

patch.description: Partial update; send only the fields to change. Only the 21 StoreSettings fields are writable — anything else in the body is ignored, not an error (id and slug can never be written). currency must be a 3-letter uppercase ISO 4217 code; tax_rate is a number 0-100; tax_enabled and tax_inclusive accept 0, 1, true or false (strings are a 400); shipping_enabled, tax_shipping and emails_enabled are STRICTLY 0 or 1 (true/false and strings are a 400 — a settings write that quietly means something else is how a store ends up shipping free, or mailing customers, without anyone deciding to); shipping_flat_amount is a non-negative INTEGER in minor units (a float is a 400, never rounded); email_log_retention_days is a non-negative INTEGER of days (0 = keep forever; a negative or fractional value is a 400). A body with nothing updatable is a 400, not a no-op 200. The tax and shipping fields are LIVE — checkout applies them from the next order on and snapshots the result; emails_enabled is also LIVE — while 1, a successful checkout emails the shopper an order confirmation and, when the store has an email set, the operator a new-order alert, and the same switch sends the shopper a payment-confirmed email when the order reaches `paid` and a status email on every subsequent transition (processing, shipped, completed, cancelled, refunded). Slice 5c-c: emails_enabled alone is not enough — mail also requires a connected Brevo account (`PUT /api/v1/email-credentials`); a store without one sends nothing. Slice 5c-d adds a fifth mail kind, refund_confirmed, sent by a call that causes NO status transition: when a stranded refund reservation confirms and its confirmed total now completes coverage of the capture, it corrects a refunded figure that status_refunded quoted too low, sent at most once per order. email_log_retention_days is also LIVE — checked once after every send batch to prune store_email_log — but nothing is actually pruned until migration 0061 has run against a given tenant's database. Only the analytics ids (google_analytics_id, facebook_pixel_id) are stored without being applied: the storefront emits them in slice 6, so do not report those as live behaviour. Served by STORE tenants with store data. On a CMS tenant the SAME path exists too: the CMS’s own /api/v1 mirror routes it to a different CMS resource, so a 200 here does not prove you are talking to a store — check GET /api/v1/users/me, whose `product` field names the product that answered. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

name.description: 1-60 characters.

logo_text.description: Header wordmark shown when there is no logo image. Empty or null falls back to the store name.

tax_enabled.description: 0 or 1. LIVE: with 1, checkout taxes the order at tax_rate under the tax_inclusive terms and snapshots both onto it. With 0 no tax is charged and the order's tax fields are 0.

tax_rate.description: Percentage, 0-100. LIVE: the rate checkout charges at while tax_enabled is 1, snapshotted onto each order as tax_rate_bp (basis points).

tax_inclusive.description: 0 or 1. LIVE: 0 = the listed prices EXCLUDE tax and it is added on top (order total = subtotal + shipping + tax); 1 = the listed prices already CONTAIN it and the order records the tax extracted out of them (total = subtotal + shipping).

shipping_enabled.description: 0 or 1, default 0. LIVE: with 1, checkout collects a delivery address (line1, city, postcode and a 2-letter country are then REQUIRED — see POST /api/shop/checkout) and charges shipping_flat_amount, snapshotting both onto the order. With 0 no address is collected, no shipping line is shown anywhere, and orders record shipping_amount 0. Strictly 0 or 1 — true/false and '1' are a 400, unlike the tax flags.

shipping_flat_amount.description: Integer MINOR units (500 = 5.00), default 0, never negative. LIVE: the store-wide flat delivery charge applied while shipping_enabled is 1. A float is a 400, not rounded. 0 with shipping enabled is a real configuration — the store ships free and says so.

tax_shipping.description: 0 or 1, default 0. LIVE: whether the delivery charge is taxed. Tax is computed on ONE base with ONE rounding — subtotal + (tax_shipping ? shipping_amount : 0) — never on the goods and the delivery separately, which can differ by a minor unit. Strictly 0 or 1.

emails_enabled.description: Default 0. LIVE (slice 5c-a): while 1, a successful checkout emails the shopper an order confirmation and — when the store has an email address set — the operator a new-order alert. Slice 5c-b adds, to the same switch: a payment-confirmed email when the order reaches `paid` (by gateway callback or by the operator recording receipt), and a status email on every subsequent transition (`processing`, `shipped`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `refunded`). Each is sent once, by the call that actually caused the transition, and every attempt is recorded. Both render the ORDER's own snapshot, so a later settings change cannot rewrite a receipt that was already sent. Slice 5c-c: this toggle no longer implies a sender. Mail now requires a connected account (`PUT /api/v1/email-credentials`) and is sent from THAT account's own verified address and name — never a shared platform address. A store with this set to 1 but no connected account sends nothing; every attempt is still recorded, as `skipped` with `no_credentials`. A send that fails is likewise recorded and never affects the order.

google_analytics_id.description: Stored only in this release; emitted by the storefront in slice 6.

facebook_pixel_id.description: Stored only in this release; emitted by the storefront in slice 6.

gateway_mode.description: Which gateway credential rows checkout uses, store-wide: 'test' (default — a store that has not chosen cannot accidentally take live cards) or 'live'. Never selectable per request.

get.description: The privacy jurisdictions this merchant has declared itself subject to (P6): {data: [{jurisdiction_id, basis, declared_at}], available: [{id, name}]}, `data` ordered by id and `available` by name. A declaration is the merchant's own assertion — the privacy engine treats it as a `configured` signal, authoritative because the merchant carries the obligation — and is NOT personal data. `data` is empty until the merchant declares one; `available` is every jurisdiction id (and its human name) the PUT below will accept — the same ledger table it validates against (P10 task 7), so an operator does not have to guess one of the 32 ids.

put.description: REPLACE the declared set with the body's {jurisdictions: [{jurisdiction_id, basis?}]} — ids missing from the body are WITHDRAWN (audited privacy.jurisdiction.withdraw), new ids or a changed basis are DECLARED (audited privacy.jurisdiction.declare), unchanged rows are left alone; [] clears the set. basis is 'manual' (default) or 'threshold_test' (the merchant assessed a US-state doing-business + revenue/volume threshold); 'origin_country' is a system basis and is refused. Every jurisdiction_id is validated against the privacy jurisdiction ledger and the whole request is refused on the first unknown one (400 unknown_jurisdiction:<id>) — nothing persists, so a typo can never sit in the profile unnoticed. Other 400s: unknown_field:<name>, invalid_jurisdiction, invalid_basis:<id>, duplicate_jurisdiction:<id>. Returns the new set in the GET shape.

get.description: What the privacy rule pack says about the storefront's OWN trackers (P7): {data: [{rule_key, jurisdiction_id, confidence, enforcement, source_url, source_authority, value_json}]}, one row per (rule key, jurisdiction) in force now, for exactly the rule keys the tracker inventory references (five today) — both the rule that argues a cookie is exempt from consent and the rule that argues it is not. get.description: Whether this supplier has a stored AliExpress credential — write-only, exactly like /api/v1/gateway-credentials and /api/v1/email-credentials. Returns configured metadata ONLY: app_key (plaintext), expires_at, configured_at. app_secret and access_token are NEVER returned by this or any other endpoint — there is no read-back call. No master-key gate: a missing platform encryption key must never stop an operator seeing whether a credential is configured. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route — the call returns 404 (or 401 when authentication fails first) and never store data. Authenticated with a store PAT; READ-ONLY PATs MAY NOT CALL THIS: the read is itself the privileged act, so a read-only token is 403 read_only_token in the middleware (changed in spec 1.31.0 — it was permitted before). A full-access PAT or a cookie session reads it normally.

put.description: Store (create or replace) this supplier's AliExpress credential. Body is exactly {app_key, app_secret, access_token} — every field a non-empty string of 1-500 characters, trimmed, and rejected (400) if it contains a control character; an unknown field is a 400 unknown_field:<name>. Refused (400 supplier_has_no_adapter) for a 'manual' supplier — there is no adapter to use a credential with, and storing a secret nothing can read is a security surface with no benefit. Success body is {"success": true, "configured": true} and nothing more. 503 supplier_credentials_unavailable until the platform encryption key (GATEWAY_MASTER_KEY) is configured — same precedent as gateway/email credentials, never a 500. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET.

post.description: Pulls current cost and stock from AliExpress onto up to 25 of this supplier's LINKED products (supplier_external_id set), never-synced products first and then the longest-unsynced, so repeated calls make progress through a whole catalogue instead of re-touching the same 25. NOTHING IS SCHEDULED — there is no cron and no background job; a sync happens ONLY when this endpoint is called. Writes ONLY cost_price, supplier_stock and supplier_synced_at on each touched product — it NEVER writes stock (that column alone drives reservation, oversell and backorder logic and decides what the storefront will sell). supplier_stock is what the supplier REPORTED, not the store's sellable stock. A per-item cost more than 10x the product's own price is refused as skipped/cost_out_of_range rather than trusted (a guard against a unit-mismatch in the adapter's assumptions, not a real price change) — that product's stored cost_price is left untouched. One product's failure never abandons the rest of the batch: each item in results reports its own outcome. This adapter is UNVERIFIED — built with no real AliExpress credentials to test against — so confirm with POST .../verify before telling a store owner this is working. Served by STORE tenants only (product: "store" from GET /api/store); a CMS tenant has no such route. Authenticated with a store PAT; read-only tokens may only GET (a read-only token gets 403 on this POST).

200.description: The batch ran (individual items may still have failed or been skipped — see results)

synced.description: Products in this batch whose cost_price/supplier_stock/supplier_synced_at were written.

skipped.description: Products in this batch refused for a specific reason (currently only cost_out_of_range) — nothing was written for them.

failed.description: Products in this batch whose AliExpress call itself failed (network error, malformed response, provider error) — nothing was written for them.

remaining.description: Linked products still due for a sync (never synced, or last synced over 24h ago) that THIS batch did not touch. Above 0 means call this endpoint again to make further progress.

reason.description: Present for skipped/failed rows only — e.g. cost_out_of_range, or the (capped, secret-stripped) provider error for a failed row.

post.description: "Test connection": makes ONE real call to AliExpress using this supplier's stored credential. NEVER a 5xx for a bad credential: a wrong app secret or an expired token is the caller's problem to fix, reported as {success: false, error: 'verification_failed', message} with the provider's own message capped to 200 characters and with the credential's own secret/token stripped out first — never the secret itself, and never an uncaught exception surfaced as a raw 500. get.description: Whether a TaxJar token is stored, per mode — {provider: "taxjar", configured: {test, live}}. The token itself is NEVER returned by any endpoint; there is no read-back call. No master-key gate. READ-ONLY PATs MAY NOT CALL THIS: the read is itself the privileged act, so a read-only token is 403 read_only_token in the middleware (changed in spec 1.31.0 — it was permitted before). A full-access PAT or a cookie session reads it normally.

put.description: Store (create or replace) the TaxJar API token for one mode — the row checkout uses is the one matching the store's gateway_mode. Sealed at rest like payment credentials; the success body is {"success": true, "configured": true} and nothing more. 503 gateway_credentials_unavailable until the platform encryption key is configured. Audited as tax.credentials.set (provider + mode only).

200.description: Stored. The token is never echoed back.

delete.description: Delete the stored TaxJar token for ?mode=test|live (optional ?provider=taxjar). 404 when none is stored. No master-key gate. Audited as tax.credentials.delete.

get.description: List all templates for this store, ordered by updated_at DESC, id DESC. Returns counts by type.

post.description: Create a new template. A default 'main' zone is automatically seeded. The slug must be unique (409 on duplicate).

slug.description: URL-safe identifier (a-z0-9-, max 100 chars). Must be unique across templates.

name.description: Display name (1-200 chars)

400.description: Invalid input (body_required, unknown_field, invalid_slug, invalid_name, invalid_type, invalid_description, invalid_parent_template_id, parent_template_not_found)

409.description: Slug already exists

post.description: Apply an action (publish, unpublish, delete) to multiple templates at once. Up to 500 IDs per call. All-or-nothing for invalid IDs — if any ID is invalid, the entire request is rejected. The layout template is the same all-or-nothing abort (409) as before. A system template (system_key non-null) named in a delete or unpublish request is different: unlike the layout, it does NOT abort the batch — it is skipped and reported in the response's `skipped` array (reason system_template_cannot_be_deleted or system_template_cannot_be_unpublished) while the rest of the requested ids still apply.

applied.description: Number of templates the action was applied to

skipped.description: Templates named in the request but not acted on because they are system templates (system_key non-null) — one entry per id, for a delete or unpublish action only. Always present; empty when nothing was skipped.

400.description: Invalid input (body_required, unknown_action, template_ids_required, invalid_template_ids, too_many_ids, missing_or_invalid_ids)

409.description: Refused as a whole, nothing applied: delete names a default+published template (cannot_delete_default_published) or the layout (cannot_delete_layout); unpublish names the layout (layout_cannot_be_unpublished, with a message)

get.description: Get a single template with its nested zones and block instances (draft + published, split into separate arrays).

patch.description: Update a template. Accepts partial payload — only supplied fields are updated. Zones and blocks are upserted (id=omit to insert). Block config is validated against the block type's schema. On a system template (system_key non-null) a blocks payload must keep exactly one instance of that system_key's required functional block (cart→cart-items, checkout→checkout-form, checkout-return→order-receipt, search→search-results, blog→post-list, blog-post→post-body, 404→heading) — same shape as the layout's one page-slot rule — or the route it resolves has nothing to render (400 system_template_needs_one_block). Only enforced when the payload touches blocks; a patch that omits `blocks` leaves the existing set alone.

400.description: Invalid input (invalid_zone, invalid_block, invalid_config, invalid_zone_slug, max_blocks_exceeded, unknown_zone, etc.). Custom CSS the sanitizer refuses: `template_custom_css: <reason>` for the template row, `invalid_block_config:<slug>:custom_css: <reason>` for a block. On the layout template (is_layout=1) also: layout_cannot_be_default, layout_cannot_have_parent, layout_needs_one_page_slot (the draft block set must contain exactly one page-slot). On a system template (system_key non-null) also: system_template_needs_one_block (the draft block set must contain exactly one instance of that system_key's required functional block; the response also carries `required` naming it).

409.description: Slug already exists or zone slug already exists

delete.description: Delete a template. Cannot delete default+published templates (409 cannot_delete_default_published), the layout template (409 cannot_delete_layout — unpublish it instead), or a system template (409 system_template_cannot_be_deleted — system_key non-null; deleting it would self-heal on the next fan-out via the seed, but the operator's content would be lost in the meantime with no warning, so it is blocked outright).

409.description: Cannot delete default or published template (cannot_delete_default_published), the layout template (cannot_delete_layout), or a system template (system_template_cannot_be_deleted)

post.description: Create a copy of a template with a new slug and name. The duplicate is created in draft status.

409.description: Slug already exists

post.description: Generate a short-lived preview token for this template, plus the storefront URL to open it on. The URL depends on the template: home and the layout template preview on `/`, product-detail and category on the first live product/category (404 `no_products_for_preview` / `no_categories_for_preview` when the store has none), all-products on `/products`, and every other custom template on `/pages/{slug}`. A system template (system_key non-null) previews on its own fixed route instead: `cart` on `/cart`, `search` on `/search`, `blog` on `/blog`, `blog-post` on the first published post (`/blog/{slug}`; 404 `no_posts_for_preview` when the store has none), `checkout` (404 `no_cart_for_preview` — there is no live cart to render against) and `checkout-return` (404 `no_order_for_preview` — there is no real order to render against). `404` owns no URL at all — it answers every path that matches nothing — so there is no address to mint a token against, and it returns 404 `no_url_for_preview`; preview it by publishing it and visiting any dead path. The layout and every system-page system_key are deliberately NOT sent to `/pages/{slug}`: the storefront resolver refuses them there, so such a link would always 404.

404.description: Template not found, or no product/category/post available for preview context (no_products_for_preview, no_categories_for_preview, no_posts_for_preview), or a system page whose preview needs state the API can't fabricate (no_cart_for_preview on checkout, no_order_for_preview on checkout-return) or no URL at all (no_url_for_preview on 404)

post.description: Publish a template. Promotes all draft blocks to published, archives any blocks they displace, and increments the published_version counter.

Unpublish a template: reverts it and its published blocks to draft. published_version and published_at are kept as the record of the last publish. The layout template (is_layout=1) cannot be unpublished — every storefront page renders through it — and answers 409 layout_cannot_be_unpublished with a message. A system template (system_key non-null) also cannot be unpublished (409 system_template_cannot_be_unpublished): its route (e.g. /blog) is fixed and unpublishing would 404 it permanently — the seed's INSERT OR IGNORE can re-create a missing row on the next fan-out but cannot heal one that exists in draft status.

409.description: Layout template cannot be unpublished (layout_cannot_be_unpublished; the body also carries a human-readable message), or a system template cannot be unpublished (system_template_cannot_be_unpublished)

get.description: Uniform product discovery: BOTH products serve this path. Returns the caller's own user row (never includes credential columns) plus `readOnly` — true when authenticating with a read-only PAT — `authMethod` (`pat` or `session`), and `product` ("cms" or "store"), which tells you which sections of this API the tenant serves. Make it the first call of every session. On CMS tenants it is the /api/v1 mirror of /api/users/me, so PATCH /api/v1/users/me works there too — documented once at PATCH /api/users/me, like every CMS operation. On store tenants only this /api/v1 path exists, and only as GET: PATCH is a 404 (a read-only token is refused first with 403 read_only_token).

product.description: Which EdgePress product this tenant runs: "cms" (absent also means cms) or "store".

readOnly.description: True when the presented PAT is read-only.

patch.description: Update the caller's own user row. **CMS tenants only** — the v1 path mirrors PATCH /api/users/me on a CMS. Store tenants serve GET at this path but not PATCH, and return 404 not_found for it; see GET /api/store for the store tenant's profile.

404.description: Not found. Returned by store tenants, which do not support PATCH at this path.

409.description: A zone with that slug already exists

delete.description: Delete a zone and every block in it (prevents orphan data). Requires role editor or above; a lower-privileged token gets 403. Idempotent: an unknown id still returns 204, not 404.

204.description: Deleted (or already absent — deletes are idempotent)

post.description: Applies the design's templates, its starter pages (only those listed) and the theme, in one atomic write. A starter page whose slug already exists replaces it only while that page is still the untouched setup placeholder (its publication status is kept); any other existing page is skipped, never overwritten. Existing posts are never modified; with removeSamples, the sample posts created at setup (and only those) are deleted in the same write.
